sentences.zh: 【晉紀十七】 起玄黓執徐，盡強圉作噩，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 17] From Xuanyi Zhixu through Qiangyu Zuoe, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Jin, Number Seventeen] Spanning from the cyclical year Xuanyi Zhixu through Qiangyu Zuoe—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹和七年（

translations.literal: Under the Radiant Ancestor Emperor Cheng, middle period upper section, seventh year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, seventh year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元三三二年）

translations.literal: renchen year, AD 332)
translations.idiomatic: the year renchen, AD 332)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinwei, a great amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day xinwei, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 趙主勒大饗群臣，謂徐光曰：「朕可方自古何等主？」

translations.literal: The Zhao ruler Shi Le gave a great feast for his ministers and said to Xu Guang: "With whom among the ancient rulers may I be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao ruler Shi Le held a grand feast for his ministers and asked Xu Guang, "Which of the ancient rulers am I fit to be compared with?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下神武謀略過於漢高，後世無可比者。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and strategic planning surpass Emperor Gao of Han; none in later ages can be compared."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang answered, "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and strategic genius surpass even Emperor Gaozu of Han; no one in later ages can compare."

sentences.zh: 勒笑曰：「人豈不自知！

translations.literal: Shi Le laughed and said: "Can a man truly not know himself!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le laughed and said, "Surely a man knows himself!

sentences.zh: 卿言太過。

translations.literal: Your words go too far.
translations.idiomatic: You flatter me too much.

sentences.zh: 朕若遇漢高祖，當北面事之，與韓、彭比肩；

translations.literal: If I met Emperor Gao of Han, I would serve him facing north, standing shoulder to shoulder with Han Xin and Peng Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Had I met Emperor Gaozu of Han, I would have served him as his vassal, ranking alongside Han Xin and Peng Yue;

sentences.zh: 若遇光武，當並驅中原，未知鹿死誰手。

translations.literal: if I met Emperor Guangwu, we would race across the Central Plains together, and it would be unknown whose hand the deer would die in.
translations.idiomatic: but had I met Emperor Guangwu, we would have contended for the Central Plains side by side—and who would have won the prize, no one could say.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫行事，宜礌礌落落，如日月皎然，終不效曹孟德、司馬仲達欺人孤兒、寡婦，狐媚以取天下也。」

translations.literal: A great man in his conduct should be open and forthright, bright as sun and moon; he would never imitate Cao Mengde and Sima Zhongda in deceiving orphans and widows and using sycophancy to seize the realm."
translations.idiomatic: A true man should act with open grandeur, bright as the sun and moon—never imitating Cao Cao and Sima Yi, who preyed on orphans and widows and wheedled their way to empire."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆頓首稱萬歲。

translations.literal: All the ministers bowed their heads and shouted "Long live Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers bowed low and shouted their acclamations.

sentences.zh: 勒雖不學，好使諸生讀書而聽之，時以其意論古今得失，聞者莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Although Shi Le was unlearned, he liked to have scholar-officials read books aloud for him to hear; he would often discuss the gains and losses of past and present according to his own understanding, and those who heard him were all pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shi Le had little formal learning, he loved to have scholars read aloud to him and would often offer his own views on the rights and wrongs of history; all who heard him were won over.

sentences.zh: 嘗使人讀《漢書》，聞酈食其勸立六國後，驚曰：「此法當失，何以遂得天下？」

translations.literal: Once he had someone read the Book of Han; hearing that Li Yiji urged establishing the descendants of the Six States, he exclaimed in alarm: "With this policy he ought to have lost—how then did he finally gain the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, hearing the Book of Han read aloud, he was startled when Li Yiji's advice to restore the six states came up. "That policy should have lost him the empire," he cried—"how did he still win the realm?"

sentences.zh: 及聞留侯諫，乃曰：「賴有此耳！」

translations.literal: When he heard the Marquis of Liu's remonstrance, he then said: "He owed it to this alone!"
translations.idiomatic: When he heard how the Marquis of Liu dissuaded him, he said, "He was saved only by that!"

sentences.zh: 郭敬之退戍樊城也，晉人復取襄陽。

translations.literal: When Guo Jing withdrew to garrison Fancheng, the Jin forces again recovered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Jing withdrew to garrison Fancheng, the Jin recovered Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，敬復攻拔之，留戍而歸。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Guo Jing attacked and captured it again, left a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Guo Jing attacked and took it again, left troops to hold it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 趙右僕射程遐言於趙主勒曰：「中山王勇悍權略，群臣莫及；

translations.literal: Zhao Right Vice Director Cheng Xia said to the Zhao ruler Shi Le: "The Prince of Zhongshan is brave, fierce, and skilled in power and strategy; none among the ministers can match him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Right Vice Director Cheng Xia said to Shi Le, "The Prince of Zhongshan is bold, ruthless, and masterful in strategy—no minister can match him;

sentences.zh: 觀其志，自陛下之外，視之蔑如；

translations.literal: judging by his intent, apart from Your Majesty he regards everyone as beneath notice;
translations.idiomatic: by his bearing, he holds everyone but Your Majesty in contempt;

sentences.zh: 加以殘賊安忍，久為將帥，威振外內，其諸子年長，皆典兵權；

translations.literal: added to this, he is cruel and ruthless, has long served as commander, his prestige shakes within and without, his sons are grown, and all hold military authority;
translations.idiomatic: he is cruel by nature, has commanded armies for years, and his prestige dominates court and camp alike; his grown sons all command troops;

sentences.zh: 陛下在，自當無它，恐非少主之臣也。

translations.literal: while Your Majesty lives, there will naturally be no other trouble, but I fear he will not be a subject fit for a young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: while you live, all may yet be well—but I doubt he will prove a loyal servant to a young heir.

sentences.zh: 宜早除之，以便大計。」

translations.literal: He should be removed early to facilitate the great design."
translations.idiomatic: He should be removed now, for the sake of the dynasty's future.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「今天下未安，大雅沖幼，宜得強輔。

translations.literal: Shi Le said: "The realm is not yet secure, and Daya is young; he ought to have a strong supporter.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le replied, "The realm is still unsettled, and Daya is only a child—he needs a strong protector.

sentences.zh: 中山王骨肉至親，有佐命之功，方當委以伊、霍之任，何至如卿所言！

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan is bone and flesh, closest kin, and has merit in aiding the mandate; he should be entrusted with a role like Yi Yin and Huo Guang—how could it be as you say!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan is my own kin and helped found the state; I mean to entrust him with a regency like Yi Yin or Huo Guang—how can it be as you say!

sentences.zh: 卿正恐不得擅帝舅之權耳；

translations.literal: You are simply afraid you will not be able to monopolize the power of the emperor's maternal uncle;
translations.idiomatic: You only fear you will not keep your monopoly as the emperor's uncle-in-law;

sentences.zh: 吾亦當參卿顧命，勿過憂也。」

translations.literal: I too will include you in the deathbed charge—do not worry excessively."
translations.idiomatic: I will name you among the regents as well—do not fret so much."

sentences.zh: 遐泣曰：「臣所慮者公家，陛下乃以私計拒之，忠言何自而入乎！

translations.literal: Cheng Xia wept and said: "What I worry about is the public house; Your Majesty rejects it with private calculations—how can loyal words ever enter!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia wept and said, "I speak for the state, yet Your Majesty dismisses me with private suspicions—how can honest counsel ever reach you?

sentences.zh: 中山王雖為皇太后所養，非陛下天屬，雖有微功，陛下酬其父子恩榮亦足矣，而其志願無極，豈將來有益者乎！

translations.literal: Although the Prince of Zhongshan was raised by the Empress Dowager, he is not Your Majesty's kin by Heaven's line; though he has slight merit, Your Majesty's repayment of favor and glory to father and son is already enough, yet his ambitions are boundless—can he be of benefit in the future!
translations.idiomatic: Though the Empress Dowager raised the Prince of Zhongshan, he is not your blood kin; you have already rewarded his service more than enough, yet his ambitions know no limit—will he truly serve the heir?

sentences.zh: 若不除之，臣見宗廟不血食矣。」

translations.literal: If he is not removed, I foresee the ancestral temple receiving no blood offerings."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not remove him, I see the ancestral temple left without sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 勒不聽。

translations.literal: Shi Le would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 遐退，告徐光，光曰：「中山王常切齒於吾二人，恐非但危國，亦將為家禍也。」

translations.literal: Cheng Xia withdrew and told Xu Guang; Guang said: "The Prince of Zhongshan constantly gnashes his teeth at the two of us—I fear he will bring disaster not only to the state but also to our families."
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Xia withdrew, he told Xu Guang, who said, "The Prince of Zhongshan already bears us a grudge—I fear he will ruin not only the state but our families as well."

sentences.zh: 它日，光承間言於勒曰：「今國家無事，而陛下神色若有不怡，何也？」

translations.literal: Another day, Guang seized an opportunity to say to Shi Le: "The state is now at peace, yet Your Majesty's expression seems displeased—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day Xu Guang took occasion to ask Shi Le, "The realm is at peace, yet Your Majesty seems troubled—why?"

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「吳、蜀未平，吾恐後世不以吾為受命之王也。」

translations.literal: Shi Le said: "Wu and Shu are not yet pacified; I fear posterity will not regard me as a king who received the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said, "Wu and Shu are not yet subdued—I fear later ages will not count me among the true heirs of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「魏承漢運，劉備雖興於蜀，漢豈得為不亡乎！」

translations.literal: Guang said: "Wei inherited Han's fortune; though Liu Bei rose in Shu, could Han be said not to have perished!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang said, "Wei inherited Han's mandate; though Liu Bei rose in Shu, did Han not still fall?"

sentences.zh: 孫權在吳，猶今之李氏也。

translations.literal: Sun Quan in Wu is like today's Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan in Wu is no different from the Li family of today.

sentences.zh: 陛下苞括二都，平蕩八州，帝王之統不在陛下，復當在誰！

translations.literal: Your Majesty embraces the two capitals and pacifies eight provinces—if the imperial succession is not with Your Majesty, with whom else should it be!
translations.idiomatic: You hold both capitals and have pacified eight provinces—if the imperial succession is not yours, whose can it be?

sentences.zh: 且陛下不憂腹心之疾，而更憂四支乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, should Your Majesty not worry about disease of the heart and vitals, yet worry instead about the four limbs!
translations.idiomatic: Should you not worry about the disease at your heart rather than your limbs?

sentences.zh: 中山王藉陛下威略，所向輒克，而天下皆言其英武亞於陛下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan relies on Your Majesty's prestige and strategy; wherever he goes he conquers, and all under Heaven say his martial brilliance is second only to Your Majesty's.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan wins every battle under your banner, and the realm already says his prowess rivals yours.

sentences.zh: 且其資性不仁，見利忘義，父子並據權位，勢傾王室；

translations.literal: Moreover, his nature is unkind; seeing profit he forgets righteousness; father and son together hold positions of power, their momentum overturning the royal house;
translations.idiomatic: His nature is cruel; he forgets duty for gain; father and son together dominate the court, their power eclipsing the throne;

sentences.zh: 而耿耿常有不滿之心。

translations.literal: yet he constantly harbors a dissatisfied heart.
translations.idiomatic: and he nurses a perpetual grievance.

sentences.zh: 近於東宮侍宴，有輕皇太子之色。

translations.literal: Recently at a feast in the Eastern Palace he showed an air of slighting the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At a recent feast in the Eastern Palace he showed open contempt for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 臣恐陛下萬年之後，不可複製也。」

translations.literal: I fear that after Your Majesty's ten thousand years, it will not be possible to restrain him."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after Your Majesty's passing, no one will be able to control him."

sentences.zh: 勒默然，始命太子省可尚書奏事，且以中常侍嚴震參綜可否，惟征伐斷斬大事乃呈之。

translations.literal: Shi Le was silent, then for the first time ordered the crown prince to review and approve memorials to the Masters of Writing, and had the Palace Attendant Yan Zhen participate in weighing approval or rejection; only campaigns, executions, and great affairs were to be presented to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le fell silent, then ordered the crown prince to review memorials to the Masters of Writing, with Palace Attendant Yan Zhen deciding routine matters; only war, capital punishment, and major policy reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是嚴震之權過於主相，中山王虎之門可設雀羅矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan Zhen's power surpassed that of the chief minister, and at the Prince of Zhongshan Hu's gate one could have set out bird nets.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen's power now exceeded the chief minister's, and sparrows could have nested undisturbed at Prince of Zhongshan Shi Hu's gate.

sentences.zh: 虎愈怏怏不悅。

translations.literal: Hu grew ever more resentful and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu grew ever more sullen and resentful.

sentences.zh: 秋，趙郭敬南掠江西，太尉侃遣其子平西參軍斌及南中郎將桓宣乘虛攻樊城，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: In autumn, Zhao's Guo Jing raided south of the Yangzi in Jiangxi; Grand Commandant Tao Kan sent his son, the Pingxi Army Aide Bin, and the Southern Gentlemen-General Huan Xuan to strike Fancheng while the enemy was exposed, capturing all their troops.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Guo Jing of Zhao raided south of the Yangzi. Grand Commandant Tao Kan sent his son Bin, an aide on the Pingxi staff, and Southern Gentlemen-General Huan Xuan to strike Fancheng while the enemy was away and took all the garrison captive.

sentences.zh: 敬旋救樊，宣與戰於涅水，破之，皆得其所掠。

translations.literal: Guo Jing turned back to relieve Fancheng; Xuan fought him on the Nie River, defeated him, and recovered all that had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing turned back to relieve Fancheng; Huan Xuan met him on the Nie River, routed him, and recovered everything the raiders had taken.

sentences.zh: 侃兄子臻及竟陵太守李陽攻新野，拔之。

translations.literal: Tao Kan's brother's son Zhen and the Jingling Administrator Li Yang attacked Xinye and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's nephew Zhen and Jingling prefect Li Yang attacked Xinye and took it.

sentences.zh: 敬懼，遁去；

translations.literal: Guo Jing was afraid and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing fled in fear;

sentences.zh: 宣陽遂拔襄陽。

translations.literal: Xuan and Yang then captured Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: and Huan Xuan and Li Yang went on to recover Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 侃使宣鎮襄陽，宣招懷初附，簡刑罰，略威儀，勸課農桑，或載鉏耒於軺軒，親帥民芸獲。

translations.literal: Tao Kan had Xuan garrison Xiangyang; Xuan won over those newly submitted, simplified punishments, reduced ceremonial display, urged farming and sericulture, and sometimes carried hoes and plows in his light carriage, personally leading the people in weeding and harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan stationed Huan Xuan at Xiangyang, where he won over the newly submitted, eased punishments, cut back ceremony, promoted farming, and sometimes rode out in his carriage with hoe and plow to lead the people in the fields.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽十餘年，趙人再攻之，宣以寡弱拒守，趙人不能勝；

translations.literal: He was at Xiangyang more than ten years; the Zhao forces attacked twice, and Xuan with few and weak troops held them off so the Zhao could not prevail;
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years at Xiangyang the Zhao attacked twice; with scant forces he held them off each time;

sentences.zh: 時人以為亞於祖逖、周訪。

translations.literal: men of the time regarded him as second only to Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.
translations.idiomatic: and contemporaries ranked him just below Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.

sentences.zh: 成大將軍壽寇寧州，以其征東將軍費黑為前鋒，出廣漢，鎮南將軍任回出越巂，以分寧州之兵。

translations.literal: Cheng's Grand General Li Shou invaded Ning Province, with his Eastern Campaign General Fei Hei as vanguard advancing from Guanghan and the Southern Pacification General Ren Hui advancing from Yuexi to divide Ning Province's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's Grand General Li Shou invaded Ning Province. He sent Eastern Campaign General Fei Hei ahead from Guanghan and Southern Pacification General Ren Hui from Yuexi to divide the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壽、黑至朱提，朱提太守董炳城守，寧州刺史尹奉遣建寧太守霍彪引兵助之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Shou and Hei reached Zhuti; Zhuti Administrator Dong Bing defended the city, and Ning Province Inspector Yin Feng sent the Jianning Administrator Huo Biao to lead troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Shou and Hei reached Zhuti. Prefect Dong Bing held the city while Ningzhou inspector Yin Feng sent Jianning prefect Huo Biao with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 壽欲逆拒彪，黑曰：「城中食少，宜縱彪入城，共消其谷，何為拒之！」

translations.literal: Shou wished to meet and repel Biao; Hei said: "Food in the city is scant—better to let Biao enter the city and consume their grain together; why reject him!"
translations.idiomatic: Shou wanted to block Biao, but Hei said, "They have little food in the city—let Biao in so his men will eat their stores. Why turn him away?"

sentences.zh: 壽從之。

translations.literal: Shou followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shou agreed.

sentences.zh: 城久不下，壽欲急攻之。

translations.literal: The city long would not fall; Shou wished to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege dragged on, Shou wanted to storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「南中險阻難服，當以日月制之，待其智勇俱困，然後取之，溷牢之物，何足汲汲也。」

translations.literal: Hei said: "The south is rugged and hard to subdue; one should wear them down over months and years, wait until wit and courage are both exhausted, then take them—things in a privy pit, why be so eager!"
translations.idiomatic: Hei said, "The south is rugged and hard to tame—wear them down over time until wit and courage fail, then take them. Why rush after something trapped in a privy?"

sentences.zh: 壽不從，攻，果不利，乃悉以軍事任黑。

translations.literal: Shou would not follow; he attacked and indeed met with ill fortune, whereupon he entrusted all military affairs to Hei.
translations.idiomatic: Shou refused, attacked, met defeat, and then gave Hei full command.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子朔，進太尉侃為大將軍，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month renzi, Tao Kan the Grand Commandant was advanced to Grand General, permitted sword and shoes in the palace hall, not required to hasten on entering court, and not called by name in acclamation;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of renzi, Grand Commandant Tao Kan was promoted to Grand General with the privileges of wearing sword and shoes in the palace, entering court without hurrying, and being acclaimed without use of his personal name;

sentences.zh: 侃固辭不受。

translations.literal: Tao Kan firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan firmly declined the honor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，帝遷於新宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, the emperor moved to the new palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, the emperor moved into the new palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，涼州僚屬勸張駿稱涼王，領秦、涼二州牧，置公卿百官如魏武、晉文故事。

translations.literal: This year, the staff of Liang Province urged Zhang Jun to take the title King of Liang, hold the governorships of Qin and Liang provinces, and establish dukes, ministers, and the hundred offices as in the precedents of Wei Wu-di and Jin Wen-di.
translations.idiomatic: That year the officials of Liang Province urged Zhang Jun to declare himself King of Liang, govern Qin and Liang provinces, and set up a full court on the model of Cao Cao and Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 駿曰：「此非人臣所宜言也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said: "This is not what a subject ought to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said, "These are not words a loyal subject should speak.

sentences.zh: 敢言此者，罪不赦！」

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak thus, his crime shall not be pardoned!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares speak so again shall not be pardoned!"

sentences.zh: 然境內皆稱之為王。

translations.literal: Yet within his territory all called him king.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout his domain everyone called him king.

sentences.zh: 駿立次子重華為世子。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun established his second son Chonghua as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun named his second son Chonghua heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹和八年（

translations.literal: Under the Radiant Ancestor Emperor Cheng, middle period upper section, eighth year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, eighth year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 癸已，公元三三三年）

translations.literal: guisi year, AD 333)
translations.idiomatic: the year guisi, AD 333)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，成大將軍李壽拔朱提，董炳、霍彪皆降，壽威震南中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Cheng's Grand General Li Shou captured Zhuti; Dong Bing and Huo Biao both surrendered, and Shou's prestige shook the south.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Li Shou captured Zhuti; Dong Bing and Huo Biao surrendered, and his prestige dominated the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 丙子，趙主勒遣使來修好；

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the Zhao ruler Shi Le sent envoys to seek friendly relations;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Shi Le of Zhao sent envoys seeking peace;

sentences.zh: 詔焚其幣。

translations.literal: an edict ordered their gifts burned.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict ordered their tribute burned.

sentences.zh: 三月，寧州刺史尹奉降於成，成盡有南中之地，大赦，以大將軍壽領寧州。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ning Province Inspector Yin Feng surrendered to Cheng; Cheng came to possess all the lands of the south, declared a great amnesty, and had Grand General Shou oversee Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yin Feng surrendered; Cheng held all of the south, declared a general amnesty, and put Grand General Shou in charge of Ning Province.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲寅，遼東武宣公慕容廆卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jiayin, Murong Hui, Duke Wu of Liaodong, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day jiayin, Murong Hui, Duke Wu of Liaodong, died.

sentences.zh: 六月，世子皝以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the heir Murong Huang, as Pacifier of the North General acting as Ping Province governor, supervised and governed the territory within.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month heir Murong Huang, as Pacifier of the North acting governor of Ping Province, took charge of the domain.

sentences.zh: 赦系囚。

translations.literal: He pardoned prisoners in custody.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty to prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以長史裴開為軍諮祭酒，郎中令高詡為玄菟太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Chief Clerk Pei Kai Army Adviser Libationer and Master of Palace Gentlemen Gao Xu Administrator of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: He made chief clerk Pei Kai army adviser and master of palace gentlemen Gao Xu prefect of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 皝以帶方太守王誕為左長史，誕以遼東太守陽騖為才而讓之；

translations.literal: Huang made the Daifang Administrator Wang Dan Left Chief Clerk; Dan, considering the Liaodong Administrator Yang Ji talented, yielded the post to him;
translations.idiomatic: Huang named Daifang prefect Wang Dan left chief clerk, but Dan, judging Liaodong prefect Yang Ji the abler man, yielded the post to him;

sentences.zh: 皝從之，以誕為右長史。

translations.literal: Huang followed this and made Dan Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Huang agreed and made Dan right chief clerk instead.

sentences.zh: 趙主勒寢疾，中山王虎入侍禁中，矯詔，群臣親戚皆不得入；

translations.literal: The Zhao ruler Shi Le took to his bed; the Prince of Zhongshan Hu entered to attend him in the inner palace, forged edicts, and neither ministers nor kin were permitted to enter;
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le fell ill, Prince of Zhongshan Shi Hu attended him inside the palace, forged edicts, and barred ministers and kin alike;

sentences.zh: 疾之增損，外無知者。

translations.literal: whether the illness improved or worsened, those outside knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: so no one outside knew whether he improved or worsened.

sentences.zh: 又矯詔召秦王宏、彭城王堪還襄國。

translations.literal: He also forged edicts summoning the Prince of Qin Hong and the Prince of Pengcheng Kan back to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged orders recalling Princes Hong of Qin and Kan of Pengcheng to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒疾小廖，見宏，驚曰：「吾使王處籓鎮，正備今日，有召王者邪，將自來邪？

translations.literal: When Shi Le's illness eased slightly and he saw Hong, he said in alarm: "I sent you, Prince, to hold the frontier post precisely to guard against this day—was there a summons, or did you come of your own will?
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le briefly rallied and saw Hong, he exclaimed, "I posted you on the frontier for just such a day—were you summoned, or did you come on your own?

sentences.zh: 有召者，當按誅之！」

translations.literal: If there was a summons, the summoner should be punished by law!"
translations.idiomatic: If anyone summoned you, he shall answer with his life!"

sentences.zh: 虎懼曰：「秦王思慕，暫還耳，今遣之。」

translations.literal: Hu said in fear: "The Prince of Qin longed for you and returned only briefly; I am sending him back now."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, afraid, said, "Prince Hong missed you and came only briefly—I am sending him back now."

sentences.zh: 仍留不遣。

translations.literal: Yet he still detained him and would not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept Hong and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 數日，復問之，虎曰：「受詔即遣，今已半道矣。」

translations.literal: Several days later he asked again; Hu said: "Upon receiving the edict I sent him off; he is already halfway there."
translations.idiomatic: Days later Shi Le asked again; Hu said, "I sent him as soon as I received your order—he is already halfway back."

sentences.zh: 廣阿有蝗，虎密使其子冀州刺史邃帥騎三千游於蝗所。

translations.literal: There was a locust plague at Guang'e; Hu secretly had his son Sui, Inspector of Ji Province, lead three thousand horsemen to range about where the locusts were.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts struck Guang'e, Hu secretly sent his son Sui, governor of Ji Province, with three thousand cavalry to the affected region.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，勒疾篤，遺命曰：「大雅兄弟，宜善相保，司馬氏，汝曹之前車也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Shi Le's illness grew grave; his deathbed charge said: "Daya and his brothers should protect one another well; the Sima clan is your warning cart ahead on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Shi Le lay dying. His last words were, "Daya and his brothers must protect one another—the fate of the Sima clan is your warning.

sentences.zh: 中山王宜深思周、霍，勿為將來口實。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan should deeply ponder the examples of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang, and not provide material for future reproach."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhongshan, take Yi Yin and Huo Guang as your models—do not give posterity cause to condemn you."

sentences.zh: 戊辰，勒卒。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Shi Le died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen Shi Le died.

sentences.zh: 中山王虎劫太子弘使臨軒，收右光祿大夫程遐、中書令徐光，下廷尉，召邃使將兵入宿衛，文武皆奔散。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan Hu coerced Crown Prince Hong to preside at the throne hall, arrested the Right Household Grandee Cheng Xia and the Palace Secretary Xu Guang and sent them to the Minister of Justice, summoned Sui to lead troops in as palace guards, and civil and military officials all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu forced Crown Prince Hong to the throne, arrested Cheng Xia and Xu Guang and sent them to prison, called in Sui with troops as palace guard, and courtiers fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 弘大懼，自陳劣弱，讓位於虎。

translations.literal: Hong was greatly afraid, declared himself weak and unfit, and yielded the throne to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, terrified, declared himself unfit and offered the throne to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「君終，太子立，禮之常也。」

translations.literal: Hu said: "When the lord dies, the crown prince succeeds—this is the constant rule of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu said, "When the sovereign dies the heir succeeds—that is the law of ritual."

sentences.zh: 弘涕泣固讓，虎怒曰：「若不堪重任，天下自有大義，何足豫論！」

translations.literal: Hong wept and firmly yielded; Hu said angrily: "If you cannot bear the heavy charge, the realm itself has the great principle—what need to discuss it beforehand!"
translations.idiomatic: Hong wept and refused again. Shi Hu snapped, "If you cannot bear the burden, the realm will find its own remedy—why debate it now?"

sentences.zh: 弘乃即位。

translations.literal: Hong then took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then took the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 殺程遐、徐光。

translations.literal: He killed Cheng Xia and Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Cheng Xia and Xu Guang.

sentences.zh: 夜，以勒喪潛瘞山谷，莫知其處。

translations.literal: By night they secretly buried Le's coffin in a mountain valley, and no one knew the place.
translations.idiomatic: That night they secretly interred Shi Le's remains in a mountain valley, and no one knew where.

sentences.zh: 己卯，備儀衛，虛葬於高平陵，謚曰明帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: On the day jimao they prepared guards of honor and held a ceremonial burial at Gaoping Mausoleum; his posthumous title was Mingdi, and his temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao they staged a full honor guard and conducted a ceremonial burial at Gaoping Mausoleum; he was given the posthumous title Emperor Ming and the temple name High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 趙將石聰及譙郡太守彭彪，各遣使來降。

translations.literal: The Zhao generals Shi Cong and Peng Biao, Administrator of Qiao Commandery, each sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao general Shi Cong and Peng Biao, prefect of Qiao commandery, each sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 聰本晉人，冒姓石氏。

translations.literal: Cong was originally a man of Jin who had falsely taken the surname Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong was originally a Jin subject who had assumed the surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣督護喬球將兵救之，未至，聰等為虎所誅。

translations.literal: The court sent the Supervisor-Protector Qiao Qiu to lead troops to rescue them, but before he arrived Cong and the others were executed by Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court dispatched Supervisor-Protector Qiao Qiu with troops to relieve them, but before he arrived Shi Cong and his fellows were put to death by Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝遣長史勃海王濟等來告喪。

translations.literal: Murong Huang sent his Chief Clerk Wang Ji of Bohai and others to announce the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang sent his chief clerk Wang Ji of Bohai and others to announce his father's death.

sentences.zh: 八月，趙主弘以中山王虎為丞相、魏王、大單于，加九錫，以魏郡等十三郡為國，總攝百揆。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Zhao ruler Hong appointed the Prince of Zhongshan Hu Chancellor, Prince of Wei, and Grand Chanyu, granted him the Nine Bestowals, made Wei Commandery and twelve other commanderies his state, and put all government affairs under his control.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhao's ruler Shi Hong named the Prince of Zhongshan, Shi Hu, chancellor, Prince of Wei, and grand chanyu, granted him the Nine Bestowals, carved out thirteen commanderies including Wei as his princedom, and placed all government under his direction.

sentences.zh: 虎赦其境內，立妻鄭氏為魏王后；

translations.literal: Hu proclaimed an amnesty within his domain and installed his wife Lady Zheng as Princess of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu declared an amnesty in his domain and made his wife Lady Zheng Princess of Wei;

sentences.zh: 子邃為魏太子，加使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: his son Sui as Heir of Wei, additionally with credentials as envoy, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, Grand General, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: his son Shi Sui as heir of Wei, with additional titles as envoy bearing the imperial staff, palace attendant, commander of all armies at home and abroad, grand general, and recorder of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 次子宣為使持節、車騎大將軍、冀州刺史，封河間王；

translations.literal: his second son Xuan as envoy with staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Jizhou, enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: his second son Xuan as envoy with staff, general of chariots and cavalry, and inspector of Jizhou, enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 韜為前鋒將軍、司隸校尉，封樂安王；

translations.literal: Tao as Vanguard General and Colonel Director of Retainers, enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an;
translations.idiomatic: Tao as vanguard general and colonel director of retainers, enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an;

sentences.zh: 遵封齊王，鑒封代王，苞封樂平王；

translations.literal: Zun was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, Jian as Prince of Dai, and Bao as Prince of Leping;
translations.idiomatic: Zun was made Prince of Qi, Jian Prince of Dai, and Bao Prince of Leping;

sentences.zh: 徙平原王斌為章武王。

translations.literal: the Prince of Pingyuan Bin was transferred to be Prince of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Pingyuan, Bin, was reassigned as Prince of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 勒文武舊臣，皆補散任；

translations.literal: Le's old civil and military officials were all assigned to empty posts;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's veteran civil and military officials were all given hollow appointments;

sentences.zh: 虎之府寮親黨，悉署台省要職。

translations.literal: Hu's staff and kin were all appointed to key posts in the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's household staff and kin filled every key post at court.

sentences.zh: 以鎮軍將軍夔安領左僕射，尚書郭殷為右僕射。

translations.literal: The Pacifying-the-Army General Kui An was made acting Left Vice Director, and the Master of Writing Guo Yin Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The pacifying-the-army general Kui An was named acting left vice director, and Master of Writing Guo Yin right vice director.

sentences.zh: 更命太子宮曰崇訓宮，太后劉氏以下皆徙居之。

translations.literal: The crown prince's palace was renamed the Palace of Exalted Instruction, and the Empress Dowager Lady Liu and all below her were moved to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's palace was renamed the Palace of Exalted Instruction, and Empress Dowager Liu and everyone beneath her were relocated there.

sentences.zh: 選勒宮人及車馬、服玩之美者，皆入丞相府。

translations.literal: The finest palace women, chariots, horses, and ornaments of Le were selected and all entered the Chancellor's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The finest of Shi Le's palace women, carriages, horses, and luxuries were taken into the chancellor's residence.

sentences.zh: 宇文乞得歸為其東部大人逸豆歸所逐，走死於外。

translations.literal: Wenyan Qidedegui was driven out by Yidougui, the eastern chieftain of his tribe, and fled to die abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyan Qidedegui was expelled by Yidougui, chieftain of the eastern branch of his tribe, and fled to his death in exile.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝引兵討之，軍於廣安；

translations.literal: Murong Huang led troops to attack him and encamped at Guang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang marched against him and encamped at Guang'an;

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。

translations.literal: Yidougui in fear sued for peace, whereupon he built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui, alarmed, sued for peace; Murong Huang then built the fortresses of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 成建寧、牂柯二郡來降，李壽復擊取之。

translations.literal: The two commanderies of Jianning and Zangke in Cheng submitted, and Li Shou attacked and recovered them.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng commanderies of Jianning and Zangke submitted, but Li Shou struck back and retook them.

sentences.zh: 趙劉太后謂彭城王堪曰：「先帝甫晏駕，丞相遽相陵籍如此。

translations.literal: The Zhao Empress Dowager Lady Liu said to the Prince of Pengcheng Kan: "The late emperor has only just passed away, and already the Chancellor so hastily bullies and insults us in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Empress Dowager Liu said to the Prince of Pengcheng, Kan, "Our late emperor has only just died, and already the chancellor bullies us like this.

sentences.zh: 帝祚之亡，殆不復久。

translations.literal: The destruction of the imperial line cannot be far off.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's end cannot be far away.

sentences.zh: 王將若之何？」

translations.literal: What will Your Highness do about it?"
translations.idiomatic: What will you do?"

sentences.zh: 堪曰：「先帝舊臣，皆被疏斥，軍旅不復由人，宮省之內，無可為者；

translations.literal: Kan said: "The late emperor's old officials have all been pushed aside; military affairs are no longer in anyone else's hands, and within the palace precincts nothing can be done;
translations.idiomatic: Kan replied, "The late emperor's old ministers have all been cast aside; no one else controls the armies anymore, and inside the palace there is nothing we can do;

sentences.zh: 臣請奔兗州，挾南陽王恢為盟主，據廩丘，宣太后詔於牧、守、征、鎮，使各舉兵以誅暴逆，庶幾猶有濟也。」

translations.literal: your servant asks to flee to Yanzhou, take the Prince of Nanyang Hui as covenant leader, hold Linqiu, proclaim the Empress Dowager's edict to the governors, prefects, expeditionary commanders, and garrison commanders, and have each raise troops to punish the violent rebel—perhaps there may still be success."
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to flee to Yanzhou, rally the Prince of Nanyang, Hui, as our leader, seize Linqiu, and proclaim Your Majesty's edict to every governor, prefect, and regional commander, calling on each to raise troops against this tyrant—there may yet be hope."

sentences.zh: 劉氏曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: Lady Liu said: "The matter is urgent!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu said, "There is no time to lose!

sentences.zh: 當速為之。」

translations.literal: You must act quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Act at once."

sentences.zh: 九月，堪微服、輕騎襲兗州，不克，南奔譙城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Kan in plain dress with a light escort raided Yanzhou but failed, and fled south to Qiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kan, in disguise and with a small mounted force, struck at Yanzhou but failed and fled south to Qiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 丞相虎遣其將郭太追之，獲堪於城父，送襄國，炙而殺之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Hu sent his general Guo Tai in pursuit, captured Kan at Chengfù, sent him to Xiangguo, and killed him by roasting.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Shi Hu sent his general Guo Tai in pursuit, seized Kan at Chengfù, sent him to Xiangguo, and killed him by slow roasting.

sentences.zh: 征南陽王恢還襄國。

translations.literal: He summoned the Prince of Nanyang Hui back to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled the Prince of Nanyang, Hui, to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 劉氏謀洩，虎廢而殺之，尊弘母程氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: Lady Liu's plot leaked out; Hu deposed and killed her and honored Hong's mother Lady Cheng as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu's plot was exposed, Shi Hu deposed and killed her and elevated Hong's mother, Lady Cheng, to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 堪本田氏子，數有功，趙主勒養以為子。

translations.literal: Kan was originally a son of the Tian clan who had repeatedly won merit; the Zhao ruler Le adopted him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was originally a Tian clansman who had won repeated distinction; Shi Le had adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 劉氏有膽略，勒每與之參決軍事，佐勒建功業，有呂後之風，而不□石忌更過之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu had courage and resource; Le often consulted with her in deciding military affairs, and she aided Le in building his enterprise, with something of Empress Lü's spirit, but Shi Hu's jealousy of her went even further.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu was bold and shrewd; Shi Le had often consulted her on military affairs, and she had helped him build the state in the manner of Empress Lü—yet Shi Hu's jealousy of her went even further.

sentences.zh: 趙河東王生鎮關中，石朗鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: The Zhao Prince of Hedong Sheng garrisoned Guanzhong, and Shi Lang garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Prince of Hedong, Sheng, held Guanzhong, and Shi Lang held Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，生、朗皆舉兵以討丞相虎；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Sheng and Lang both raised troops to attack the Chancellor Hu;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Sheng and Lang both took up arms against Chancellor Shi Hu;

sentences.zh: 生自稱秦州刺史，遣使來降。

translations.literal: Sheng styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou and sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng declared himself inspector of Qinzhou and sent envoys to submit to Jin.

sentences.zh: 氐帥蒲洪自稱雍州刺史，西附張駿。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Pu Hong styled himself Inspector of Yongzhou and attached himself to Zhang Jun in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Pu Hong declared himself inspector of Yongzhou and threw in his lot with Zhang Jun in the west.

sentences.zh: 虎留太子邃守襄國，將步騎七萬攻朗於金墉；

translations.literal: Hu left the Heir Apparent Sui to guard Xiangguo and led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Lang at Jinyong;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu left the heir Sui to hold Xiangguo and marched seventy thousand foot and horse to attack Lang at Jinyong;

sentences.zh: 金墉潰，獲朗，刖而斬之；

translations.literal: Jinyong fell; he captured Lang, cut off his feet, and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong collapsed; he took Lang prisoner, mutilated him, and beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 進向長安，以梁王挺為前鋒大都督。

translations.literal: he advanced toward Chang'an and made the Prince of Liang Ting Grand Vanguard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed on toward Chang'an, naming the Prince of Liang, Ting, grand vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 生遣將軍郭權帥鮮卑涉瑰眾二萬為前鋒以拒之，生將大軍繼發，軍於蒲阪。

translations.literal: Sheng sent the general Guo Quan to lead twenty thousand Xianbei of the Shegui tribe as vanguard to resist him; Sheng followed with the main army and encamped at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent General Guo Quan ahead with twenty thousand Xianbei of the Shegui tribe as vanguard, then followed with the main army and encamped at Puban.

sentences.zh: 權與挺戰於潼關，大破之，挺及丞相左長史劉隗皆死，虎還奔澠池，枕屍三百餘里。

translations.literal: Quan fought Ting at Tong Pass and routed him utterly; Ting and the Chancellor's Left Chief Clerk Liu Wei both died; Hu fled back toward Mianchi, and corpses lay stacked for more than three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Quan met Ting at Tong Pass and shattered his army; Ting and the chancellor's left chief clerk Liu Wei were both killed; Shi Hu fled toward Mianchi, and the dead lay thick for more than three hundred li along the road.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑潛與虎通謀，反擊生。

translations.literal: The Xianbei had secretly entered a pact with Hu and turned to strike Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei had secretly made common cause with Shi Hu and turned on Sheng.

sentences.zh: 生不知挺已死，懼，單騎奔長安。

translations.literal: Sheng did not know Ting was already dead; in fear he fled alone on horseback to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, unaware that Ting was dead, panicked and rode alone to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 權收餘眾，退屯渭汭。

translations.literal: Quan gathered the remnant forces and withdrew to encamp at the bend of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Quan rallied the survivors and fell back to the bend of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 生遂棄長安，匿於雞頭山。

translations.literal: Sheng then abandoned Chang'an and hid on Mount Jitou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then abandoned Chang'an and hid on Mount Jitou.

sentences.zh: 將軍蔣英據長安拒守，虎進兵擊英，斬之。

translations.literal: The general Jiang Ying held Chang'an in defense; Hu advanced and attacked Ying and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: General Jiang Ying held Chang'an in defiance; Shi Hu advanced, struck him down, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 生麾下斬生以降；

translations.literal: Sheng's own followers beheaded Sheng to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's own men slew him and surrendered;

sentences.zh: 權奔隴右。

translations.literal: Quan fled to Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan fled into Longyou.

sentences.zh: 虎分命諸將屯汧、隴，遣將軍麻秋討蒲洪。

translations.literal: Hu assigned various generals to garrison Qian and Long and sent the general Ma Qiu to attack Pu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu posted his generals along Qian and Long and sent General Ma Qiu against Pu Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪帥戶二萬降於虎，虎迎拜洪光烈將軍、護氐校尉。

translations.literal: Hong led twenty thousand households in surrender to Hu; Hu met him and appointed him General of Glorious Martiality and Colonel Protector of the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Hong led twenty thousand households in submission; Shi Hu received him and named him general of glorious martiality and colonel protector of the Di.

sentences.zh: 洪至長安，說虎徙關中豪傑及氐、羌以實東方，曰：「諸氐皆洪家部曲，洪帥以從，誰敢違者！」

translations.literal: When Hong reached Chang'an he urged Hu to move the eminent families of Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang to strengthen the east, saying: "All the Di are retainers of Hong's house—if Hong leads them in following, who would dare disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an, Pu Hong urged Shi Hu to relocate Guanzhong's leading families and the Di and Qiang to populate the east, saying, "Every Di band is my household's following—if I lead them, who would dare refuse?"

sentences.zh: 虎從之，徙秦、雍民及氐、羌十餘萬戶於關東。

translations.literal: Hu agreed and moved more than a hundred thousand households of the people of Qin and Yong and of the Di and Qiang to the lands east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu agreed and moved more than a hundred thousand households from Qin and Yong, Di and Qiang alike, east of the passes.

sentences.zh: 以洪為龍驤將軍、流民都督，使居枋頭；

translations.literal: He made Hong Dragon-Courser General and Commander of Displaced Populations and had him dwell at Fangtou;
translations.idiomatic: He made Pu Hong dragon-courser general and commander of displaced populations, with his seat at Fangtou;

sentences.zh: 以羌帥姚弋仲為奮武將軍、西羌大都督，使帥其眾數萬徙居清河之灄頭。

translations.literal: he made the Qiang chieftain Yao Yaochong General of Stirring Martiality and Grand Commander of the Western Qiang and had him lead his several tens of thousands to move and dwell at Shantou in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: and he made the Qiang chieftain Yao Yaochong stirring-martiality general and grand commander of the western Qiang, ordering him to relocate his tens of thousands of followers to Shantou in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 虎還襄國，大赦。

translations.literal: Hu returned to Xiangguo and declared a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu returned to Xiangguo and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 趙主弘命虎建魏台，一如魏武王輔漢故事。

translations.literal: The Zhao ruler Hong ordered Hu to establish the Wei headquarters, following the precedent of King Wu of Wei assisting Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ruler Hong ordered Shi Hu to set up a Wei administration, on the model of King Wu of Wei assisting the Han.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝初嗣位，用法嚴峻，國人多不自安，主簿皇甫真切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: When Murong Huang first succeeded to the throne he applied the law with stern severity; many in the state were ill at ease, and the Registrar Huangfu Zhen remonstrated earnestly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang first took the throne his laws were harsh, and the people were uneasy; his registrar Huangfu Zhen remonstrated forcefully, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 皝庶兄建威將軍翰、母弟征虜將軍仁，有勇略，屢立戰功，得士心，季弟昭，有才藝；

translations.literal: Huang's elder brother by a concubine, the Establishing Might General Han, and his younger brother by the same mother, the Campaigning against Captives General Ren, were brave and resourceful, repeatedly won battle merit, and won the hearts of the officers; a youngest brother Zhao had talent and learning;
translations.idiomatic: Huang's elder half-brother, Establishing Might General Han, and his younger uterine brother, Campaigning-against-Captives General Ren, were bold and clever, won repeated victories, and held the loyalty of the troops; their youngest brother Zhao was gifted and cultivated;

sentences.zh: 皆有寵於廆。

translations.literal: all had been favored by Hui.
translations.idiomatic: all had been favorites of Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 皝忌之，翰歎曰：「吾受事於先公，不敢不盡力，幸賴先公之靈，所向有功，此乃天贊吾國，非人力也。

translations.literal: Huang was jealous of them; Han sighed and said: "I received my commission from the late lord and dared not fail to exert myself; fortunately, relying on the late lord's spirit, wherever I turned I had success—this was Heaven aiding our state, not human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang resented them. Han sighed and said, "I served our late father and gave him my utmost; thanks to his blessing I won wherever I fought—that was Heaven aiding our state, not my own prowess.

sentences.zh: 而人謂吾之所辦，以為雄才難制，吾豈可坐而待禍邪！」

translations.literal: Yet men say that what I have accomplished shows a heroic talent hard to control—how can I sit and await disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet men credit my deeds to a talent too great to tolerate—am I to sit still and wait for ruin?"

sentences.zh: 乃與其子出奔段氏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled with his son to the Duan clan.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with his son to the Duan.

sentences.zh: 段遼素聞其才，冀收其用，甚愛重之。

translations.literal: Duan Liao had long heard of his talent and hoped to employ him, and treated him with great favor and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao had long admired his ability and hoped to win his service, and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 仁自平郭來奔喪，謂昭曰：「吾等素驕，多無禮於嗣君，嗣君剛嚴，無罪猶可畏，況有罪乎！」

translations.literal: Ren came from Pingguo to attend the mourning and said to Zhao: "We have long been arrogant and often showed disrespect to the heir—he is stern and severe; even without guilt he is to be feared, how much more when there is guilt!"
translations.idiomatic: Ren came from Pingguo for the funeral and said to Zhao, "We have always been proud and often rude to the new lord. He is harsh—even the innocent have reason to fear him, let alone the guilty!

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「吾輩皆體正嫡，於國有分。

translations.literal: Zhao said: "We are all born of the legitimate principal wife and have a share in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao replied, "We are all sons of the legitimate line and have a claim on the realm.

sentences.zh: 兄素得士心，我在內未為所疑，伺其間隙，除之不難。

translations.literal: Elder Brother has long won the hearts of the officers; I am within and not yet suspected—watch for an opening and removing him will not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: You have always held the troops' loyalty; inside the capital I am not yet suspect—wait for an opening and removing him will not be difficult.

sentences.zh: 兄趣舉兵以來，我為內應，事成之日，與我遼東。

translations.literal: Elder Brother, hurry and raise troops to come; I will act as inner collaborator, and when the affair succeeds give me Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Brother, raise your forces and march; I will act from within. When we succeed, Liaodong is mine.

sentences.zh: 男子舉事，不克則死，不能效建威偷生異域地。」

translations.literal: When a man undertakes a great affair, if he does not succeed he dies—he cannot imitate the Establishing Might General in stealing life in a foreign land."
translations.idiomatic: When a man takes such a stand, he wins or he dies—I will not imitate Establishing Might and skulk out his days in a foreign land."

sentences.zh: 仁曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Ren said: "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: Ren said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 遂還平郭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 閏月，仁舉兵而西。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Ren raised troops and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Ren raised his army and marched west.

sentences.zh: 或以仁、昭之謀告皝，皝未之信，遣使按驗。

translations.literal: Someone reported Ren and Zhao's plot to Huang; Huang did not believe it and sent an envoy to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Murong Huang of Ren and Zhao's plot; he did not believe it and sent an envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 仁兵已至黃水，知事露，殺使者，還據平郭。

translations.literal: Ren's army had already reached Huangshui; learning that the matter was exposed, he killed the envoy and returned to hold Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Ren's army had already reached Huangshui; when he learned the plot was exposed, he killed the envoy and fell back on Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 皝賜昭死，遣軍祭酒封弈慰撫遼東，以高詡為廣武將軍，將兵五千與庶弟建武將軍幼、稚、廣威將軍軍、寧遠將軍汗、司馬遼東佟壽共討仁。

translations.literal: Huang granted Zhao death, sent the Army Libationer Feng Yi to reassure Liaodong, and appointed Gao Xu General of Expansive Martiality; leading five thousand troops together with his younger brothers the Establishing Martiality General You, Zhi, the Expansive Might General Jun, the Pacifying-the-Distance General Han, and the Liaodong Major-domo Tong Shou, he jointly attacked Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang ordered Zhao to take his own life and sent army libationer Feng Yi to pacify Liaodong; he named Gao Xu general of expansive martiality and sent five thousand men with his younger brothers Establishing Martiality You, Zhi, Expansive Might Jun, Pacifying-the-Distance Han, and Liaodong major-domo Tong Shou to crush Ren.

sentences.zh: 與仁戰於汶城北，皝兵大敗，幼、稚、軍皆為仁所獲。

translations.literal: They fought Ren north of Wen City; Huang's army was utterly defeated, and You, Zhi, and Jun were all captured by Ren.
translations.idiomatic: They met Ren north of Wen City; Murong Huang's force was routed, and You, Zhi, and Jun were all taken.

sentences.zh: 壽嘗為仁司馬，遂降於仁。

translations.literal: Shou had once been Ren's major-domo and thereupon surrendered to Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Shou had once served Ren as major-domo and now went over to him.

sentences.zh: 前大農孫機等舉遼東城以應仁。

translations.literal: The former Grand Minister of Agriculture Sun Ji and others raised Liaodong city in response to Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand minister of agriculture Sun Ji and others rose in Liaodong city to join Ren.

sentences.zh: 封弈不得入，與汗俱還。

translations.literal: Feng Yi could not enter and returned together with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi could not enter the city and withdrew with Han.

sentences.zh: 東夷校尉封抽、護軍平原乙逸、遼東相太原韓矯皆棄城走，於是仁盡有遼東之地；

translations.literal: the Colonel of the Eastern Yi Feng Chou, the Protector of the Army Yiyi of Pingyuan, and the Administrator of Liaodong Han Jiao of Taiyuan all abandoned their cities and fled; thereupon Ren came to possess all the territory of Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of the Eastern Yi Feng Chou, Protector of the Army Yiyi of Pingyuan, and Liaodong Administrator Han Jiao of Taiyuan all abandoned their posts and fled; Ren now held all of Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 段遼及鮮卑諸部皆與仁遙相應援。

translations.literal: Duan Liao and the various Xianbei tribes all responded to Ren from afar in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao and the Xianbei tribes all rallied to Ren from afar.

sentences.zh: 皝追思皇甫真之言，以真為平州別駕。

translations.literal: Huang recalled Huangfu Zhen's words and appointed Zhen Acting Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang recalled Huangfu Zhen's warning and appointed him acting governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，郭權據上邽，遣使來降；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Guo Quan held Shanggui and sent envoys to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guo Quan held Shanggui and sent envoys to submit;

sentences.zh: 京兆、新平、扶風、馮翊、北地皆應之。

translations.literal: Jingzhao, Xinping, Fufeng, Fengyi, and Beidi all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao, Xinping, Fufeng, Fengyi, and Beidi all rose in his support.

sentences.zh: 初，張駿欲假道於成以通表建康，成主雄不許。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Jun had wished to borrow a route through Cheng to send a memorial to Jiankang; the Cheng ruler Xiong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Jun had sought passage through Cheng to send a memorial to the Jin court at Jiankang, but Cheng's ruler Li Xiong refused.

sentences.zh: 駿乃遣治中從事張淳稱籓於成以假道；

translations.literal: Jun thereupon sent his Attendant Clerk Zhang Chun to declare himself a vassal of Cheng in order to borrow the route;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun then sent his attendant clerk Zhang Chun to declare vassalage to Cheng in order to obtain the route;

sentences.zh: 雄偽許之，將使盜覆諸東峽。

translations.literal: Xiong falsely agreed and was about to have bandits overturn his boat in the eastern gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong pretended to agree and planned to have robbers capsize his boat in the eastern gorge.

sentences.zh: 蜀人橋贊密以告淳，淳謂雄曰：「寡君使小臣行無跡之地，萬里通誠於建康者，以陛下嘉尚忠義，能成人之美故也。

translations.literal: The man of Shu Qiao Zan secretly informed Chun; Chun said to Xiong: "Our lord sent this petty official to travel trackless regions and convey sincerity to Jiankang from ten thousand li away because Your Majesty honors loyalty and righteousness and can fulfill others' worthy designs.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu man named Qiao Zan secretly warned Zhang Chun. Chun told Li Xiong, "My lord sent me across trackless country ten thousand li to bear his loyalty to Jiankang because he believed Your Majesty honored righteousness and would help another fulfill a noble aim.

sentences.zh: 若欲殺臣者，當斬之都市，宣示眾目曰：『涼州不忘舊德，通使琅邪，主聖臣明，發覺殺之。』

translations.literal: If you wish to kill your servant, you ought to behead him in the market and proclaim before the multitude: 'Liangzhou did not forget old virtue and sent an envoy to Langye; the ruler is sage and the minister enlightened—they detected and executed him.'
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to kill me, do it in the open market and proclaim to all: 'Liangzhou remembered old ties and sent an envoy to Langye; our sage ruler and wise ministers uncovered the plot and put him to death.'

sentences.zh: 如此，則義聲遠播，天下畏威。

translations.literal: In that way righteous fame would spread far and all under Heaven would fear your authority.
translations.idiomatic: That way your righteous name would travel far and the realm would tremble at your power.

sentences.zh: 今使盜殺之江中，威刑不顯，何足以示天下乎！」

translations.literal: Now to have bandits kill him in mid-river—your aweful punishment would not be displayed; how could that suffice to show all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: But to have thieves murder me on the river—where is the majesty in that? How would that impress the world?"

sentences.zh: 雄大驚曰：「安有此邪！」

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly alarmed and said: "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was startled and said, "Surely there is no such plan!"

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉景騫言於雄曰：「張淳壯士，請留之。」

translations.literal: The Colonel Director of Retainers Jing Qian said to Xiong: "Zhang Chun is a stalwart man—please keep him."
translations.idiomatic: Colonel director of retainers Jing Qian said to Li Xiong, "Zhang Chun is a man of mettle—keep him here."

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「壯士安肯留！

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Would a stalwart man be willing to stay!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong said, "A man like that will never stay!

sentences.zh: 且試以卿意觀之。」

translations.literal: For now try to observe him according to your own mind."
translations.idiomatic: Try him yourself and see."

sentences.zh: 騫謂淳曰：「卿體豐大，天熱，可且遣下吏，小住須涼。」

translations.literal: Qian said to Chun: "Your build is large and stout; the weather is hot—you may first send down your subordinate officials and stay a little while until it cools."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Qian told Zhang Chun, "You are a big man, and the heat is fierce—send your clerks ahead and rest here until the weather turns cooler."

sentences.zh: 淳曰：「寡君以皇輿播越，梓宮未返，生民塗炭，莫之振救，故遣淳通誠上都。

translations.literal: Chun said: "Our lord, because the imperial carriage has been driven into exile, the late emperor's coffin has not returned, and the living people are in utter misery with none to rescue them, therefore sent Chun to convey sincerity to the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun said, "My lord, with the imperial house driven into exile, the late emperor's coffin still unreclaimed, and the people drowning in misery with no one to save them, sent me to bear his loyalty to the court at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 所論事重，非下吏所能傳；

translations.literal: The matters discussed are weighty—not something subordinate officials can convey;
translations.idiomatic: The business at hand is grave—no clerk can carry it;

sentences.zh: 使下吏可了，則淳亦不來矣。

translations.literal: if subordinate officials could settle it, then Chun would not have come either.
translations.idiomatic: had a clerk sufficed, I would not be here at all.

sentences.zh: 雖火山湯海，猶將赴之，豈寒暑之足憚哉！」

translations.literal: Even were there volcanoes and seas of boiling water, I would still go—how could mere heat and cold be worth fearing!"
translations.idiomatic: I would cross seas of fire and boiling water—how could mere heat and cold make me flinch!"

sentences.zh: 雄謂淳曰：「貴主英名蓋世，土險兵強，何不亦稱帝自娛一方？」

translations.literal: Xiong said to Chun: "Your esteemed lord's heroic name covers the age, his territory is rugged and his soldiers strong—why not also declare yourself emperor and enjoy yourself in one region?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong said to Zhang Chun, "Your lord's fame towers over the age, his lands are rugged and his armies strong—why not declare yourself emperor and rule your corner in peace?"

sentences.zh: 淳曰：「寡君祖考以來，世篤忠貞，以仇恥未雪，枕戈待旦，何自娛之有！」

translations.literal: Chun said: "From our lord's ancestors down, our house has been steadfast in loyalty; with enmity and shame yet unavenged, he keeps his spear beside his pillow awaiting dawn—how could there be any thought of self-indulgence!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun said, "From his forebears our lord's house has been steeped in loyalty; with shame and vengeance still unpaid, he sleeps with a spear at his pillow awaiting dawn—what room is there for self-indulgence!"

sentences.zh: 雄甚慚，曰：「我之祖考本亦晉臣，遭天下大亂，與六郡之民避難此州，為眾所推，遂有今日。

translations.literal: Xiong was deeply ashamed and said: "My own ancestors were originally also Jin subjects; encountering great chaos in the realm, we fled with the people of six commanderies to this province, were pushed forward by the multitude, and thus came to today.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was deeply ashamed and said, "My forebears too were Jin subjects; when the realm fell into chaos we fled here with the people of six commanderies, were pressed forward by the multitude, and so came to what we are today.

sentences.zh: 琅邪若能中興大晉於中國者，亦當帥眾輔之。」

translations.literal: If Langye can restore Great Jin in the Central Lands, I too shall lead the masses to assist."
translations.idiomatic: If Langye can restore Great Jin in the Central Plains, I too shall lead my forces to aid him."

sentences.zh: 厚為淳禮而遣之。

translations.literal: He treated Chun generously and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhang Chun with great courtesy and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 淳卒致命於建康。

translations.literal: Chun ultimately delivered his charge at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun at last fulfilled his mission at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 長安之失守也，敦煌計吏耿訪自漢中入江東，屢上書請遣大使慰撫涼州。

translations.literal: When Chang'an fell, the Dunhuang accounting clerk Geng Fang entered Jiangdong from Hanzhong and repeatedly memorialized asking that a great envoy be sent to comfort and pacify Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, Geng Fang, an accounting clerk from Dunhuang, came east from Hanzhong into the lower Yangtze region and repeatedly petitioned the court to send a high envoy to comfort and reassure Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以訪守侍書御史，拜張駿鎮西大將軍，選隴西賈陵等十二人配之。

translations.literal: The court appointed Fang acting Imperial Secretary, invested Zhang Jun as Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and selected twelve men including Jia Ling of Longxi to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Geng Fang acting imperial secretary, invested Zhang Jun as Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and chose twelve men including Jia Ling of Longxi to go with him.

sentences.zh: 訪至梁州，道不通，以詔書付賈陵，詐為賈客以達之。

translations.literal: Fang reached Liang Province but the road was blocked; he entrusted the imperial edict to Jia Ling, who disguised himself as a merchant to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Fang reached Liang Province but the route was cut; he handed the imperial edict to Jia Ling, who posed as a merchant to get through.

sentences.zh: 是歲，陵始至涼州，駿遣部曲督王豐等報謝。

translations.literal: That year Jia Ling finally reached Liangzhou; Zhang Jun sent his retainers' commander Wang Feng and others to return thanks.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jia Ling at last reached Liangzhou; Zhang Jun sent his retinue commander Wang Feng and others back with thanks.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹和九年（

translations.literal: Under the Radiant Ancestor Emperor Cheng, middle period upper section, ninth year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, ninth year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元三三四年）

translations.literal: jiawu year, AD 334)
translations.idiomatic: the year jiawu, AD 334)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，趙改元延熙。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhao changed its era name to Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Zhao adopted the era name Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 詔以郭權為鎮西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Guo Quan General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Guo Quan General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 仇池王楊難敵卒，子毅立，自稱龍驤將軍、左賢王、下辨公；

translations.literal: The Chouchi king Yang Nandisou died; his son Yi succeeded, styling himself General of Dragon Cavalry, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xia Bian;
translations.idiomatic: The Chouchi king Yang Nandisou died; his son Yi succeeded him, styling himself General of Dragon Cavalry, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xia Bian;

sentences.zh: 以叔父堅頭之子盤為冠軍將軍、右賢王、河池公，遣使來稱籓。

translations.literal: he appointed his uncle Jiantou's son Pan General Who Establishes Might, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi, and sent envoys to declare himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Pan, son of his uncle Jiantou, General Who Establishes Might, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi, and sent envoys to submit as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁卯，詔遣耿訪、王豐繼印綬授張駿大將軍、都督陝西、雍、秦、涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingmao, an edict sent Geng Fang and Wang Feng to follow up with seals and cords investing Zhang Jun as Grand General and area commander of the military affairs of Shaanxi, Yong, Qin, and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day dingmao, an edict sent Geng Fang and Wang Feng with seals and cords to invest Zhang Jun as Grand General and commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Yong, Qin, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲使者不絕。

translations.literal: From then on envoys came every year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on envoys traveled back and forth every year without interruption.

sentences.zh: 慕容仁以司馬翟楷領東夷校尉，前平州別駕龐鑒領遼東相。

translations.literal: Murong Ren had his marshal Zhai Kai serve as Colonel of the Eastern Yi and former Pingzhou registrar Pang Jian serve as Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ren had his marshal Zhai Kai serve as Colonel of the Eastern Yi and the former Pingzhou registrar Pang Jian as Administrator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 段遼遣兵襲徒河，不克；

translations.literal: Duan Liao sent troops to raid Tuhe but failed;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao sent troops to raid Tuhe but failed;

sentences.zh: 復遣其弟蘭與慕客翰共攻柳城，柳城都尉石琮、城大慕輿泥並力拒守，蘭等不克而退。

translations.literal: he again sent his younger brother Lan and Murong Han jointly to attack Liucheng; Liucheng Commandant Shi Cong and the city chief Murong Ni together stoutly defended, and Lan and the others could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: he again sent his younger brother Lan and Murong Han to attack Liucheng together; Commandant Shi Cong and city chief Murong Ni defended with combined strength, and Lan's forces could not prevail and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遼怒，切責蘭等，必令拔之。

translations.literal: Liao was furious and harshly rebuked Lan and the others, insisting they must take it.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao was furious, sharply rebuked Lan and the others, and ordered them to take the city at all costs.

sentences.zh: 休息二旬，復益兵來攻。

translations.literal: After resting twenty days, they gathered more troops and came again to attack.
translations.idiomatic: After resting twenty days, they reinforced their army and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 士皆重袍蒙楯，作飛梯，四面俱進，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: The soldiers all wore heavy coats and covered their shields, built flying ladders, and advanced on all four sides day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wore heavy coats, shielded their heads, raised siege ladders, and pressed the assault from all four sides day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 琮、泥拒守彌固，殺傷千餘人，卒不能拔。

translations.literal: Shi Cong and Murong Ni defended ever more stoutly, killing and wounding over a thousand; in the end they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong and Murong Ni held ever more firmly, killing and wounding more than a thousand men, and in the end the attackers could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝遣慕容汗及司馬封弈等共救之。

translations.literal: Murong Huang sent Murong Khan and Registrar Feng Yi and others jointly to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang sent Murong Khan, Registrar Feng Yi, and others to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 皝戒汗曰：「賊氣銳，勿與爭鋒！」

translations.literal: Huang warned Khan: "The enemy's spirit is sharp—do not contend with their edge!"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang warned Murong Khan, "The enemy's spirit is keen—do not meet them head-on!"

sentences.zh: 汗性驍果，以千餘騎為前鋒，直進。

translations.literal: Khan was fierce and resolute by nature; with over a thousand cavalry as the vanguard he pressed straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Khan was bold and resolute by nature; he took more than a thousand horsemen as vanguard and charged straight ahead.

sentences.zh: 封弈止之，汗不從。

translations.literal: Feng Yi tried to stop him, but Khan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi tried to stop him, but Murong Khan would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 與蘭遇於牛尾谷，汗兵大敗，死者太半；

translations.literal: They met Lan at Niwei Valley; Khan's army was utterly defeated, more than half the men dead;
translations.idiomatic: They met Duan Lan at Niwei Valley; Murong Khan's army was routed and more than half his men were killed;

sentences.zh: 弈整陳力戰，故得不沒。

translations.literal: Feng Yi arrayed his troops and fought with all his strength, and so they were not annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi re-formed the line and fought with all his strength, and so the force was not wiped out.

sentences.zh: 蘭欲乘勝窮追，慕容翰恐遂滅其國，止之曰：「夫為將當務慎重，審己量敵，非萬全不可動。

translations.literal: Lan wished to press the pursuit while victory was hot; Murong Han feared this would destroy their state and stopped him, saying: "A general must be prudent, measure himself and the enemy—one must not move without absolute certainty.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lan wished to pursue while the advantage held; Murong Han, fearing their state would be destroyed, stopped him and said, "A commander must be cautious, sizing up himself and the enemy—he must not move unless the odds are sure.

sentences.zh: 今雖挫其偏師，未能屈其大勢。

translations.literal: Though we have now checked their flank force, we have not yet bent their main strength.
translations.idiomatic: We have checked only a flank force today, not broken their main power.

sentences.zh: 皝多權詐，好為潛伏，若悉國中之眾自將以拒我，我縣軍深入，眾寡不敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Huang is full of stratagems and loves ambush; if he leads the entire nation's forces himself to resist us, we advance deep with our army suspended far from home, few against many—that is the path of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang is full of stratagems and loves ambush; if he leads the whole nation's forces against us himself, we will be an army deep in hostile country, few against many—that is the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 且受命之日，正求此捷；

translations.literal: Moreover, from the day we received our orders, this victory is exactly what was sought;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, from the day we received our orders, this victory is precisely what was required;

sentences.zh: 若違命貪進，萬一取敗，功名俱喪，何以返面！」

translations.literal: if we disobey orders and greedily advance, and should we by any chance fail, both fame and achievement are lost—how could we show our faces on return!"
translations.idiomatic: if we disobey orders and press on from greed, and should we fail, fame and achievement are lost together—how could we ever show our faces again!"

sentences.zh: 蘭曰：「此已成擒，無有餘理，卿正慮遂滅卿國耳！

translations.literal: Lan said: "They are already as good as captured—there is no other possibility; you are simply afraid they will wipe out your state!
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lan said, "They are as good as taken—there is no other outcome; you only fear they will wipe out your country!

sentences.zh: 今千年在東，若進而得志，吾將迎之以為國嗣，終不負卿，使宗廟不祀也。」

translations.literal: Now Qiannian is in the east; if we advance and succeed, I shall welcome him to be heir of the state and will never fail you, so that your ancestral temples are not cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Qiannian is in the east now; if we advance and prevail, I shall welcome him as heir to the state and will never fail you, so your ancestral temples are not left without sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 千年者，慕容仁小字也。

translations.literal: Qiannian was Murong Ren's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Qiannian was Murong Ren's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「吾投身相依，無復還理；

translations.literal: Han said: "I have cast my lot with you and there is no road back;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han said, "I have cast my lot with you and there is no turning back;

sentences.zh: 國之存亡，於我何有！

translations.literal: whether the state lives or perishes—what is that to me!
translations.idiomatic: whether the state lives or dies—what is that to me!

sentences.zh: 但欲為大國之計，且相為惜功名耳。」

translations.literal: I only wish to plan for the great state and to spare your shared glory, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I only mean to plan for the great state and to spare your shared glory, that is all.

sentences.zh: 乃命所部欲獨還，蘭不得已而從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered his command to withdraw alone; Lan had no choice but to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered his command to withdraw on its own; Duan Lan had no choice but to follow.

sentences.zh: 三月，成主雄分寧州置交州，以霍彪為寧州刺史，爨深為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, Cheng ruler Xiong divided Ningzhou to establish Jiaozhou, appointing Huo Biao as Inspector of Ningzhou and Cuan Shen as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Cheng ruler Li Xiong split off Jiaozhou from Ningzhou, appointing Huo Biao Inspector of Ning and Cuan Shen Inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 趙丞相虎遣其將郭敖及章武王斌，帥步騎四萬西擊郭權，軍於華陰；

translations.literal: Zhao Chancellor Hu sent his generals Guo Ao and Prince of Zhangwu Bin leading forty thousand infantry and cavalry west to attack Guo Quan, encamping at Huayin;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chancellor Shi Hu sent his generals Guo Ao and Prince of Zhangwu Bin with forty thousand foot and horse west against Guo Quan, encamping at Huayin;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，上邽豪族殺權以降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the powerful clans of Shanggui killed Quan and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the powerful families of Shanggui killed Guo Quan and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 虎徙秦州三萬餘戶於青、並二州。

translations.literal: Hu relocated more than thirty thousand households of Qinzhou to Qing and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu moved more than thirty thousand Qinzhou households to Qing and Bing.

sentences.zh: 長安人陳良夫奔黑羌，與北羌王薄句大等侵擾北地、馮翊。

translations.literal: Chen Liangfu of Chang'an fled to the Black Qiang and with the Northern Qiang king Bo Judda and others harassed Beidi and Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liangfu of Chang'an fled to the Black Qiang and, with the Northern Qiang king Bo Judda and others, raided Beidi and Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 章武王斌、樂安王韜合擊，破之，句大奔馬蘭山。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Bin and Prince of Le'an Tao jointly attacked and defeated them; Judda fled to Malan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Bin and Prince of Le'an Tao attacked together and defeated them; Judda fled to Malan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 郭敖乘勝逐北，為羌所敗，死者什七八。

translations.literal: Guo Ao pursued north while victory was hot and was defeated by the Qiang; seven or eight tenths of his men died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ao pursued the fleeing enemy and was beaten by the Qiang; seven or eight men in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 斌等收軍還三城。

translations.literal: Bin and the others gathered their army and returned to Sancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and the others withdrew their forces to Sancheng.

sentences.zh: 虎遣使誅郭敖。

translations.literal: Hu sent an envoy to execute Guo Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent an envoy to execute Guo Ao.

sentences.zh: 秦王宏有怨言，虎幽之。

translations.literal: King of Qin Hong murmured complaints; Hu imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: King of Qin Shi Hong murmured complaints; Shi Hu had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 慕容仁自稱平州刺史、遼東公。

translations.literal: Murong Ren styled himself Inspector of Pingzhou and Duke of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ren styled himself Inspector of Pingzhou and Duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 長沙桓公陶侃，晚年深以滿盈自懼，不預朝權，屢欲告老歸國，佐吏等苦留之。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan of Changsha Tao Kan, in his later years deeply feared fullness and decline, did not participate in court power, and repeatedly wished to report old age and return home; his aides bitterly detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuan of Changsha Tao Kan, in his later years, deeply feared the peril of excess; he took no part in court power and repeatedly sought to retire and return home, but his staff bitterly pressed him to stay.

sentences.zh: 六月，侃疾篤，上表遜位。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Kan's illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial yielding his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month his illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial yielding his office.

sentences.zh: 遣左長史殷羨奉送所假節、麾、幢、曲蓋、侍中貂蟬、太尉章、荊、江、雍、梁、交、廣、益、寧八州刺史印傳、棨戟；
