translations.literal: He sent Left Chief Clerk Yin Xian to return all borrowed credentials—the staff of authority, banners, canopies, attendant's cap and cicada insignia, Grand Marshal's seal, the seals and commissions of the eight provincial inspectors of Jing, Jiang, Yong, Liang, Jiao, Guang, Yi, and Ning, and the ceremonial halberds;
translations.idiomatic: He sent his left chief clerk Yin Xian to return every credential he held—the staff of authority, banners, canopies, attendant's cap and cicada insignia, the Grand Marshal's seal, the seals and commissions of the eight provincial inspectors of Jing, Jiang, Yong, Liang, Jiao, Guang, Yi, and Ning, and the ceremonial halberds;

sentences.zh: 軍資、器仗、牛馬、舟船，皆有定薄，封印倉庫，侃自加管鑰。

translations.literal: military supplies, weapons, cattle, horses, and boats all had fixed ledgers; warehouses were sealed and Kan himself affixed the keys.
translations.idiomatic: military stores, weapons, cattle, horses, and boats were all entered in ledgers; the warehouses were sealed and Tao Kan himself affixed the locks.

sentences.zh: 以後事付右司馬王愆期，加督護統領文武。

translations.literal: He entrusted later affairs to Right Marshal Wang Yanqi, adding him as Supervisor and Protector to command civil and military matters.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted subsequent affairs to his right marshal Wang Yanqi, making him supervisor and protector over civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，輿車出，臨津就船，將歸長沙，顧謂愆期曰：「老子婆娑，正坐諸君！」

translations.literal: On the day jiayin his carriage went out; he came to the ferry and boarded the boat, about to return to Changsha, and turning to Yanqi said: "This old man pacing about—it is really because of you all!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin his carriage went out; he came to the ferry and boarded the boat, bound for Changsha, and turning to Wang Yanqi said, "This old man tottering about—it's all because of you people!"

sentences.zh: 乙卯，薨於樊谿。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he died at Fanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao he died at Fanxi.

sentences.zh: 侃在軍四十一年，明毅善斷，識察纖密，人不能欺；

translations.literal: Kan had been in the army forty-one years, clear and resolute in judgment, perceptive to the finest detail—no one could deceive him;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan had served in the army forty-one years; clear, resolute, and swift in judgment, perceptive to the finest detail—no one could deceive him;

sentences.zh: 自南陵迄於白帝，數千里中，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: from Nanling to Baidi, for several thousand li, no one picked up lost goods on the road.
translations.idiomatic: from Nanling to Baidi, for several thousand li along his routes, no one picked up what another had lost on the road.

sentences.zh: 及薨，尚書梅陶與親人曹識書曰：「陶公機神明鑒似魏武，忠順勤勞似孔明，陸抗諸人不能及也。」

translations.literal: When he died, Minister Mei Tao wrote to his kinsman Cao Shi: "Lord Tao's divine insight resembles Cao Wu, his loyal obedience and diligent toil resemble Kongming—men like Lu Kang cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Minister Mei Tao wrote to his kinsman Cao Shi, "Lord Tao's divine insight resembles Cao Cao, his loyal obedience and tireless labor resemble Zhuge Liang—men like Lu Kang cannot equal him."

sentences.zh: 謝安每言：「陶公雖用法，而恆得法外意。」

translations.literal: Xie An often said: "Though Lord Tao applied the law, he always grasped the spirit beyond the letter."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An often said, "Though Lord Tao applied the law, he always grasped the spirit beyond the letter."

sentences.zh: 安，鯤之從子也。

translations.literal: An was the son of Kun's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An was the son of Xie Kun's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 成主雄生瘍於頭。

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Xiong developed sores on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng ruler Li Xiong developed sores on his head.

sentences.zh: 身素多金創，及病，舊痕皆膿潰，諸子皆惡而遠之；

translations.literal: His body had long borne many sword wounds; when ill, old scars all suppurated; all his sons detested it and kept away;
translations.idiomatic: His body had long borne many sword wounds; when he fell ill, old scars all festered; all his sons were repelled and kept their distance;

sentences.zh: 獨太子班晝夜侍側，不脫衣冠，親為吮膿。

translations.literal: only Crown Prince Ban attended day and night at his side, never removing cap or robe, personally sucking the pus.
translations.idiomatic: only Crown Prince Ban attended him day and night at his side, never removing cap or robe, personally sucking the pus from his sores.

sentences.zh: 雄召大將軍建寧王壽受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: Xiong summoned Grand General Prince of Jianning Shou to receive the testamentary edict and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong summoned Grand General Prince of Jianning Li Shou to receive the deathbed edict and assist in government.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，雄卒，太子班即位。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao Xiong died; Crown Prince Ban ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao Li Xiong died; Crown Prince Ban ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 以建寧王壽錄尚書事，政事皆委於壽及司徒何點、尚書令王瑰，班居中行喪禮，一無所預。

translations.literal: He made Prince of Jianning Shou recorder of the Masters of Writing; all government was entrusted to Shou and Minister over the Masses He Dian and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Gui; Ban occupied himself only with mourning rites and had no part in anything else.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince of Jianning Li Shou recorder of the Masters of Writing; all government was entrusted to Shou, Minister over the Masses He Dian, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Gui; Ban occupied himself only with mourning rites and took no part in affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛未，加平西將軍庾亮征西將軍、假節、都督江、荊、豫、益、梁、雍六州諸軍事、領江、豫、荊三州刺史，鎮武昌。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei General Who Pacifies the West Yu Liang was promoted to General Who Campaigns West with acting credentials, area commander of the military affairs of Jiang, Jing, Yu, Yi, Liang, and Yong provinces, holding the three provincial governorships of Jiang, Yu, and Jing, stationed at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei General Who Pacifies the West Yu Liang was promoted to General Who Campaigns West with acting credentials, made area commander of military affairs in Jiang, Jing, Yu, Yi, Liang, and Yong, and given the three provincial governorships of Jiang, Yu, and Jing, with his seat at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 亮辟殷浩為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Liang recruited Yin Hao as recorder in his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang recruited Yin Hao as recorder in his staff.

sentences.zh: 浩，羨之子也，與豫章太守褚裒、丹楊丞杜乂，皆以識度清遠，善談《老》、《易》，擅名江東，而浩尤為風流所宗。

translations.literal: Hao was the son of Xian, and together with Prefect of Yuzhang Chu Pou, Magistrate of Danyang Du Yi, all were renowned in Jiangdong for clear insight and distant bearing, skilled at discussing Laozi and the Changes, and Hao was especially the one the elegant set looked to.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao was the son of Yin Xian; he, together with Prefect of Yuzhang Chu Pou and Magistrate of Danyang Du Yi, were all famed in the lower Yangtze for clear insight and lofty bearing, skilled in discourse on the Laozi and the Changes; among them Hao was especially the darling of the refined set.

sentences.zh: 裒，略之孫；

translations.literal: Pou was the grandson of Lue;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou was the grandson of Chu Lue;

sentences.zh: 乂，錫之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi was the son of Du Xi.

sentences.zh: 桓彝嘗謂裒曰：「季野有皮裡《春秋》。」

translations.literal: Huan Yi once said to Pou: "Jiye has a Spring and Autumn Annals beneath his skin."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi once said of Chu Pou, "Jiye carries a Spring and Autumn Annals beneath his skin."

sentences.zh: 言其外無臧否而內有褒貶也。

translations.literal: Meaning that outwardly he neither approved nor condemned but inwardly had praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that outwardly Chu Pou neither praised nor blamed, yet inwardly he judged all things.

sentences.zh: 謝安曰：「裒雖不言，而四時之氣亦備矣。」

translations.literal: Xie An said: "Though Pou does not speak, the qi of the four seasons is complete in him too."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An said, "Though Chu Pou does not speak, the spirit of all four seasons is complete in him."

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，王濟還遼東，詔遣侍御史王齊祭遼東公廆，又遣謁者徐孟策拜慕容皝鎮軍大將軍、平州刺史、大單于、遼東公、持節、都督，承製封拜，一如廆故事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Wang Ji returned to Liaodong; an edict sent Censor Wang Qi to sacrifice to Duke of Liaodong Hui, and also sent Attendant Xu Meng with credentials to invest Murong Huang as General Who Guards the Army, Inspector of Pingzhou, Great Chanyu, Duke of Liaodong, with acting credentials and area command, empowered to invest and enfeoff by imperial rescript as with Hui's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Wang Ji returned to Liaodong; an edict sent Censor Wang Qi to offer sacrifice to Duke of Liaodong Murong Hui, and Attendant Xu Meng with credentials to invest Murong Huang as General Who Guards the Army, Inspector of Pingzhou, Great Chanyu, Duke of Liaodong, with acting credentials and area command, empowered to invest and enfeoff by imperial rescript as with Murong Hui's precedent.

sentences.zh: 船下馬石津，皆為慕容仁所留。

translations.literal: When the boats reached Mashijin they were all detained by Murong Ren.
translations.idiomatic: When the boats reached Mashijin they were all detained by Murong Ren.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，衛將軍江陵穆公陸曄卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuyin, Defender General Duke Mu of Jiangling Lu Ye died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day wuyin, Defender General Duke Mu of Jiangling Lu Ye died.

sentences.zh: 成主雄之子車騎將軍越屯江陽，奔喪至成都。

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Xiong's son, General of the Chariots Who Attack the Cuan Yue, was stationed at Jiangyang; he rushed back on bereavement to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue, son of Cheng ruler Li Xiong and General of the Chariots Who Attack the Cuan, was stationed at Jiangyang; he rushed back on bereavement to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 以太子班非雄所生，意不服，與其弟安東將軍期謀作亂。

translations.literal: Because Crown Prince Ban was not born of Xiong, Yue was ill content and plotted rebellion with his younger brother, General Who Pacifies the East Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Crown Prince Ban was not Li Xiong's own son, Yue was resentful and plotted rebellion with his younger brother, General Who Pacifies the East Li Qi.

sentences.zh: 班弟玝勸班遣越還江陽，以期為梁州刺史，鎮葭萌。

translations.literal: Ban's younger brother Yu advised Ban to send Yue back to Jiangyang and appoint Qi as Inspector of Liangzhou, stationed at Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: Ban's younger brother Li Yu urged Ban to send Yue back to Jiangyang and appoint Qi Inspector of Liangzhou, stationed at Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 班以未葬，不忍遣，推心待之，無所疑間，遣玝出屯於涪。

translations.literal: Ban, because the burial had not taken place, could not bear to send him away; he treated Yue with open heart without suspicion, and sent Yu out to garrison at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Ban, because the burial had not yet taken place, could not bear to send Yue away; he treated him with open trust and no suspicion, and sent Li Yu out to garrison at Fu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥朔，越因班夜哭，弒之於殯宮，並殺班兄領軍將軍都；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the month guihai, Yue took advantage of Ban's night mourning and assassinated him in the mourning palace, also killing Ban's elder brother General Who Leads the Army Du;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day guihai, Yue took advantage of Ban's night mourning and assassinated him in the mourning palace, also killing Ban's elder brother General Who Leads the Army Li Du;

sentences.zh: 矯太后任氏令，罪狀班而廢之。

translations.literal: he forged an order from the Empress Dowager Lady Ren impeaching and deposing Ban.
translations.idiomatic: he forged an order from Empress Dowager Lady Ren listing Ban's crimes and deposing him.

sentences.zh: 初，期母冉氏賤，任氏母養之。

translations.literal: Initially, Qi's mother the Lady Ran was of low birth; Empress Dowager Lady Ren had raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Qi's mother Lady Ran was of humble birth; Empress Dowager Lady Ren had raised him.

sentences.zh: 期多才藝，有令名。

translations.literal: Qi had many talents and arts and a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi had many talents and a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 及班死，眾欲立越，越奉期而立之。

translations.literal: When Ban died, the multitude wished to install Yue; Yue upheld Qi and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ban died, the court wished to install Yue; Yue upheld Qi and had him enthroned.

sentences.zh: 甲子，期即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi Qi took the emperor's throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi Li Qi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 謚班曰戾太子。

translations.literal: Ban's posthumous title was Crown Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: Ban was given the posthumous title Crown Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 以越為相國，封建寧王，加大將軍壽大都督，徙封漢王；

translations.literal: Yue was made Chancellor of State and enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning; Grand General Shou was made Grand Commander, moved and enfeoffed as Prince of Han;
translations.idiomatic: Yue was made Chancellor of State and enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning; Grand General Li Shou was made Grand Commander and transferred to the title Prince of Han;

sentences.zh: 皆錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Both were recorded as Overseers of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Both were appointed to oversee the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以兄霸為中領軍、鎮南大將軍；

translations.literal: His elder brother Ba was made Central Army Commander-in-Chief and Grand General Who Guards the South;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his elder brother Li Ba Central Army Commander-in-Chief and Grand General Who Guards the South;

sentences.zh: 弟保為鎮西大將軍、汶山太守；

translations.literal: his younger brother Bao Grand General Who Guards the West and Governor of Wenshan;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Li Bao Grand General Who Guards the West and Governor of Wenshan;

sentences.zh: 從兄始為征東大將軍，代越鎮江陽。

translations.literal: his cousin Shi Grand General Who Conquers the East, replacing Yue to garrison Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: and his cousin Li Shi Grand General Who Conquers the East, replacing Yue to garrison Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，葬雄於安都陵，謚曰武皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin Xiong was buried at Andu Mausoleum; his posthumous title was Emperor Wu, temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin Li Xiong was buried at Andu Mausoleum with the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 始欲與壽共攻期，壽不敢發。

translations.literal: Shi wished to join with Shou to attack Qi, but Shou dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi wished to join Li Shou in attacking Li Qi, but Shou dared not move.

sentences.zh: 始怒，反譖壽於期，請殺之。

translations.literal: Shi grew angry and in turn slandered Shou to Qi, asking that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi grew furious and in turn slandered Shou to Qi, asking that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 期欲籍壽以討李玝，故不許，遣壽將兵向涪。

translations.literal: Qi wished to borrow Shou's forces to attack Li Zu, so he did not consent and sent Shou with troops toward Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi wanted to use Shou's army against Li Zu, so he refused and sent Shou with troops toward Fu.

sentences.zh: 壽先遣使告玝以去就利害，開其去路，玝遂來奔。

translations.literal: Shou first sent a messenger to tell Zu the pros and cons of staying or leaving, opening his escape route; Zu then came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shou first sent envoys to explain to Zu the stakes of staying or fleeing and cleared his escape route, and Zu then defected.

sentences.zh: 詔以王玝為巴郡太守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wang Zu Governor of Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wang Zu Governor of Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 期以壽為梁州刺史，屯涪。

translations.literal: Qi made Shou Inspector of Liang province, stationed at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed Shou Inspector of Liang province and stationed him at Fu.

sentences.zh: 趙主弘自赍璽綬詣魏宮，請禪位於丞相虎。

translations.literal: The Zhao ruler Hong himself brought the imperial seal and cord to the Wei palace, requesting to abdicate in favor of Chancellor Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao ruler Shi Hong himself brought the imperial seal and cord to the Wei palace and asked to abdicate in favor of Chancellor Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「帝王大業，天下自當有議，何為自論此邪！」

translations.literal: Hu said: "The great enterprise of emperor and king—the realm ought to deliberate on it of itself; why do you raise this matter yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "The imperial enterprise is something the realm should debate on its own—why do you bring it up yourself?"

sentences.zh: 弘流涕還宮，謂太后程氏曰：「先帝種真無復遺矣！」

translations.literal: Hong wept as he returned to the palace and said to Empress Dowager Lady Cheng: "The true seed of the late emperor is gone without remainder!"
translations.idiomatic: Hong wept as he returned to the palace and told Empress Dowager Lady Cheng, "The late emperor's true line is utterly extinguished!"

sentences.zh: 於是尚書奏：「魏台請依唐、虞禪讓故事。」

translations.literal: Then the Masters of Writing memorialized: "The Wei court requests following the precedent of the abdication of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then memorialized, "The Wei court asks to follow the precedent of Yao and Shun's abdication."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「弘愚闇，居喪無禮，不可以君萬國，便當廢之，何禪讓也！」

translations.literal: Hu said: "Hong is stupid and dim; in mourning he observes no rites—he cannot rule the myriad states; he should simply be deposed—what talk of abdication!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu replied, "Hong is dull and witless and observes no mourning rites—he cannot rule the realm. Depose him at once—what talk of abdication!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，虎遣郭殷持節入宮，廢弘為海陽王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Hu sent Guo Yin bearing credentials into the palace and deposed Hong as Prince of Haiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hu sent Guo Yin with credentials into the palace and deposed Hong as Prince of Haiyang.

sentences.zh: 弘安步就車，容色自若，謂群臣曰：「庸昧不堪纂承大統，夫復何言！」

translations.literal: Hong walked calmly to the carriage, his countenance composed, and said to the assembled ministers: "I am mediocre and benighted, unfit to succeed the great succession—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Hong walked calmly to the carriage, his face composed, and told the ministers, "I am too mediocre and benighted to inherit the great succession—what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 群臣莫不流涕，宮人慟哭。

translations.literal: None of the ministers could hold back tears; palace women wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: None of the ministers could hold back tears; palace women wailed in grief.

sentences.zh: 群臣詣魏台勸進，虎曰：「皇帝者盛德之號，非所敢當，且可稱居攝趙天王。」

translations.literal: The ministers went to the Wei court to urge his advance; Hu said: "Emperor is a title of overflowing virtue—I dare not assume it; for now you may call me Acting Regent, Heavenly King of Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers went to the Wei court to urge him to take the throne. Hu said, "Emperor is a title of supreme virtue—I dare not assume it. For now call me Acting Regent, Heavenly King of Zhao."

sentences.zh: 幽弘及太后程氏、秦王宏、南陽王恢於崇訓宮，尋皆殺之。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Hong, Empress Dowager Lady Cheng, the Prince of Qin Hong, and the Prince of Nanyang Hui at Chongxun Palace; soon all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Hong, Empress Dowager Lady Cheng, the Prince of Qin Hong, and the Prince of Nanyang Hui at Chongxun Palace; soon all were killed.

sentences.zh: 西羌大都督姚弋仲稱疾不駕，虎屢召之，乃至。

translations.literal: The Grand Commander of the Western Qiang Yao Yizhong claimed illness and would not attend court; Hu summoned him repeatedly before he at last came.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commander of the Western Qiang, Yao Yizhong, claimed illness and refused to attend court; Hu summoned him repeatedly before he finally came.

sentences.zh: 正色謂虎曰：「弋仲常謂大王命世英雄，奈何把臂受托而返奪之邪？」

translations.literal: With stern countenance he said to Hu: "I have often called you, great king, a hero ordained by fate—how can you clasp arms in entrusted fellowship only to seize it back again?"
translations.idiomatic: With a stern face he said to Hu, "I have always called you a hero born for this age—how can you clasp arms in trust and then seize the throne back?"

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「吾豈樂此哉！

translations.literal: Hu said: "Do you think I relish this!
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Do you think I relish this!

sentences.zh: 顧海陽年少，恐不能了家事，故代之耳。」

translations.literal: Considering Haiyang was young, I feared he could not manage the household affairs—that is why I replaced him."
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang is young, and I feared he could not manage the realm—that is why I replaced him."

sentences.zh: 心雖不平，然察其誠實，亦不之罪。

translations.literal: Though displeased in heart, seeing his honesty he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Though displeased at heart, Hu saw his honesty and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 虎以夔安為侍中、太尉、守尚書令，郭殷為司空，韓晞為尚書左僕射，魏郡申鐘為侍中，郎闓為光祿大夫，王波為中書令。

translations.literal: Hu appointed Kui An Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong of Wei commandery Palace Attendant; Lang Kai Gentlemen-at-Dawn Grandee; Wang Bo Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Hu appointed Kui An Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong of Wei commandery Palace Attendant; Lang Kai Grandee of the Palace; and Wang Bo Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 文武封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were enfeoffed and promoted each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were enfeoffed and promoted according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 虎行如信都，復還襄國。

translations.literal: Hu traveled to Xindu, then returned again to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Hu traveled to Xindu, then returned to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝討遼東，甲申，至襄平。

translations.literal: Murong Huang campaigned against Liaodong; on jiashen he reached Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang campaigned against Liaodong; on jiashen he reached Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 遼東人王岌密信請降。

translations.literal: Wang Ji of Liaodong sent a secret letter offering surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji of Liaodong sent a secret letter offering to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師進，入城，翟楷、龐鑒單騎走，居就、新昌等縣皆降。

translations.literal: The army advanced and entered the city; Zhai Kai and Pang Jian fled each on a single horse; counties including Jujiu and Xinchang all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and entered the city; Zhai Kai and Pang Jian fled alone on horseback; the counties of Jujiu, Xinchang, and others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 皝欲悉坑遼東民，高詡諫曰：「遼東之叛，實非本圖，直畏仁凶威，不得不從。

translations.literal: Huang wished to bury alive all the people of Liaodong; Gao Xu remonstrated: "Liaodong's rebellion was not their original intent—they merely feared Ren's fierce authority and had no choice but to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Huang wished to massacre all the people of Liaodong. Gao Xu remonstrated, "Liaodong's rebellion was not their true intent—they only feared Murong Ren's brutal authority and had no choice but to follow.

sentences.zh: 今元惡猶存，始克此城，遽加夷滅，則未下之城，無歸善之路矣。」

translations.literal: Now the chief villain still lives; having just taken this city, if you hasten to exterminate them, the cities not yet taken will have no path back to goodness."
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain still lives. If you exterminate the people the moment you take this city, the cities not yet subdued will have no path back to loyalty."

sentences.zh: 皝乃止。

translations.literal: Huang then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huang then desisted.

sentences.zh: 分徙遼東大姓于棘城。

translations.literal: He relocated the great clans of Liaodong to Jicheng in separate groups.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the great clans of Liaodong to Jicheng in groups.

sentences.zh: 以杜群為遼東相，安輯遺民。

translations.literal: He appointed Du Qun Administrator of Liaodong to settle and comfort the remaining people.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Du Qun Administrator of Liaodong to settle and comfort the survivors.

sentences.zh: 十二月，趙徐州從事蘭陵朱縱斬刺史郭祥，以彭城來降，趙將王朗攻之，縱奔淮南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhu Zong of Lanling, an adjutant of Xu province in Zhao, killed Inspector Guo Xiang and offered Pengcheng in surrender; the Zhao general Wang Lang attacked him, and Zong fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhu Zong of Lanling, a staff officer of Xu province in Zhao, killed Inspector Guo Xiang and offered Pengcheng in surrender; the Zhao general Wang Lang attacked him, and Zong fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 慕容仁遣兵襲新昌，督護新興王寓擊走之，遂徙新昌入襄平。

translations.literal: Murong Ren sent troops to raid Xinchang; the Supervisor and Protector of Xinxing, Wang Yu, drove them off, then moved Xinchang into Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ren sent troops to raid Xinchang; Wang Yu, Supervisor and Protector of Xinxing, drove them off and then moved Xinchang's population into Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹康元年（

translations.literal: Middle upper section under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, first year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, middle period upper section, first year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元三三五年）

translations.literal: yiyi, CE 335)
translations.idiomatic: yiyi, CE 335)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚午朔，帝加元服。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on gengwu the first day of the month the Emperor assumed the cap and girdle of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengwu the first day of the month, the Emperor assumed the cap and girdle of adulthood.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元。

translations.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 成、趙皆大赦，成改元玉恆，趙改元建武。

translations.literal: Both Cheng and Zhao proclaimed general amnesties; Cheng changed the era to Yuheng, Zhao to Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Both Cheng and Zhao proclaimed general amnesties; Cheng changed the era name to Yuheng and Zhao to Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 成主期立皇后閻氏，以衛將軍尹奉為右丞相，驃騎將軍、尚書令王瑰為司徒。

translations.literal: The Cheng ruler Qi installed Lady Yan as empress and appointed Guard General Yin Feng Right Chancellor and Rapid-as-Thunder Cavalry General and Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Gui Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng ruler Li Qi installed Lady Yan as empress and appointed Guard General Yin Feng Right Chancellor and Rapid-as-Thunder Cavalry General and Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Gui Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎命太子邃省可尚書奏事，唯祀郊廟、選牧守、征伐、刑殺乃親之。

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao ordered Crown Prince Sui to review matters presented to the Masters of Writing that could be approved, reserving only sacrifices to heaven and earth and the ancestral temples, selection of prefects and governors, campaigns, and punishments and executions for his personal attention.
translations.idiomatic: King Hu of Zhao ordered Crown Prince Shi Sui to review routine memorials to the Masters of Writing, reserving only sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, selection of prefects and governors, campaigns, and punishments and executions for his personal attention.

sentences.zh: 虎好治宮室，鸛雀台崩，殺典匠少府任汪；

translations.literal: Hu loved to build palaces; when the Stork Terrace collapsed, he executed Director of Constructions and Palace Storehouse Master Ren Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Hu loved to build palaces; when the Stork Terrace collapsed he executed Director of Constructions and Palace Storehouse Master Ren Wang;

sentences.zh: 復使修之，倍於其舊。

translations.literal: and had it rebuilt again, twice the size of the old.
translations.idiomatic: then had it rebuilt twice its former size.

sentences.zh: 邃保母劉芝封宜城君，關預朝權，受納賄賂，求仕進者多出其門。

translations.literal: Sui's nurse Liu Zhi was enfeoffed as Lady of Yicheng; she interfered in court power, accepted bribes, and many who sought advancement went out through her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's nurse Liu Zhi was enfeoffed as Lady of Yicheng; she meddled in court affairs, accepted bribes, and many who sought office passed through her gate.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝置左、右司馬，以司馬韓矯、軍祭酒封弈為之。

translations.literal: Murong Huang established Left and Right Majors; he appointed Major Han Jiao and Army Libationer Feng Yi to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang established Left and Right Majors and appointed Major Han Jiao and Army Libationer Feng Yi to the posts.

sentences.zh: 司徒導以贏疾，不堪朝會，三月，乙酉，帝幸其府，與群臣宴於內室，拜導並拜其妻曹氏。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Dao, owing to wasting illness, could not attend court; in the third month on yiyou the Emperor visited his mansion, feasted with the ministers in the inner chamber, and bowed to Dao and also to his wife Lady Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Wang Dao, weakened by illness, could not attend court; in the third month on yiyou the Emperor visited his mansion, feasted with the ministers in the inner chamber, and bowed to Dao and also to his wife Lady Cao.

sentences.zh: 侍中孔坦密表切諫，以為帝初加元服，動宜顧禮，帝從之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Kong Tan submitted a secret memorial of sharp remonstrance, holding that the Emperor, having just assumed adulthood, his every move ought to observe propriety; the Emperor followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Kong Tan submitted a secret memorial of sharp remonstrance, arguing that the Emperor, having just come of age, ought to observe propriety in every act; the Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 坦又以帝委政於導，從容言曰：「陛下春秋已長，聖敬日躋，宜博納朝臣，諮諏善道。」

translations.literal: Tan also said, because the Emperor had entrusted government to Dao, gently: "Your Majesty's years are already grown; your sacred reverence daily ascends—you ought broadly to admit court ministers and consult them on the good Way."
translations.idiomatic: Tan also said, because the Emperor had entrusted affairs to Dao, gently, "Your Majesty's years are already full; your sacred virtue rises daily—you ought broadly to admit court ministers and consult them on the good Way."

sentences.zh: 導聞而惡之，出坦為廷尉。

translations.literal: When Dao heard of this he took offense and sent Tan out as Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao heard of this he took offense and sent Tan out as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坦不得意，以疾去職。

translations.literal: Tan, discontented, resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Discontented, Tan resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 丹楊尹桓景，為人諂巧，導親愛之。

translations.literal: Huan Jing, Governor of Danyang, was a man of flattery and craft whom Dao favored and held dear.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jing, Governor of Danyang, was a man of flattery and craft whom Dao favored.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守南斗經旬，導謂領軍將軍陶回曰：「鬥，揚州之分，吾當遜位以厭天譴。」

translations.literal: When Mars dwelt in the Southern Dipper for more than ten days, Dao said to General of the Palace Army Tao Hui: "The Dipper is the asterism of Yang province's allotment—I ought to yield my post to appease heaven's reproof."
translations.idiomatic: When Mars lingered in the Southern Dipper for more than ten days, Dao said to General of the Palace Army Tao Hui, "The Dipper is the asterism allotted to Yang province—I ought to yield my post to appease heaven's reproof."

sentences.zh: 回曰：「公以明德作輔，而與桓景造膝，使熒惑何以退捨！」

translations.literal: Hui said: "You, sir, aid the throne with bright virtue—yet you press knee to knee with Huan Jing; how is Mars to withdraw and yield!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "You aid the throne with bright virtue—yet you sit knee to knee with Huan Jing; how is Mars to withdraw!"

sentences.zh: 導深愧之。

translations.literal: Dao was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 導辟太原王濛為掾，王述為中兵屬。

translations.literal: Dao recruited Wang Meng of Taiyuan as a staff officer and Wang Shu as an aide in the Central Army section.
translations.idiomatic: Dao recruited Wang Meng of Taiyuan as a staff officer and Wang Shu as an aide in the Central Army section.

sentences.zh: 述，昶之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shu was the great-grandson of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was the great-grandson of Wang Chang.

sentences.zh: 濛不修小廉，而以清約見稱，與沛國劉惔齊名，友善。

translations.literal: Meng did not cultivate petty scruple but was famed for clarity and restraint; he was equally famed with Liu Tan of Pei and they were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Meng did not fuss over petty scruples but was famed for clarity and restraint; he was equally renowned with Liu Tan of Pei, and they were close friends.

sentences.zh: 惔常稱濛性至通而自然有節。

translations.literal: Tan often said Meng's nature was thoroughly penetrating yet naturally possessed restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Tan often said Meng's nature was thoroughly open yet naturally restrained.

sentences.zh: 濛曰：「劉君知我，勝我自知。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "Master Liu knows me better than I know myself."
translations.idiomatic: Meng said, "Master Liu knows me better than I know myself."

sentences.zh: 當時稱風流者，以惔、濛為首。

translations.literal: Among those then called men of refined bearing, Tan and Meng led.
translations.idiomatic: Among those then called men of refined bearing, Tan and Meng led the field.

sentences.zh: 述性沈靜，每坐客辯論蜂起，而述處之恬如也。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was deep and still; whenever guests in a gathering buzzed with debate, Shu remained in it tranquil as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's nature was deep and still; whenever guests in a gathering buzzed with debate, Shu remained tranquil amid it all.

sentences.zh: 年三十，尚未知名，人謂之癡。

translations.literal: At thirty he was still not known by reputation; people called him a dullard.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he was still unknown; people called him a dullard.

sentences.zh: 導以門地辟之。

translations.literal: Dao recruited him for his family's standing.
translations.idiomatic: Dao recruited him for his family's standing.

sentences.zh: 既見，唯問在東米價，述張目不答。

translations.literal: Once they met, Dao asked only the price of rice in the east; Shu stared wide-eyed and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting Dao asked only the price of rice in the east; Shu stared wide-eyed and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 導曰：「王掾不癡，人何言癡也！」

translations.literal: Dao said: "Staff Officer Wang is no dullard—why do people call him one!"
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "Staff Officer Wang is no dullard—why do people call him one!"

sentences.zh: 嘗見導每發言，一坐莫不讚美，述正色曰：「人非堯、舜，何得每事盡善！」

translations.literal: Once when Dao spoke and every man in the seat praised him without exception, Shu said with stern countenance: "Men are not Yao or Shun—how can every matter be wholly good!"
translations.idiomatic: Once when Dao spoke and every man at the table praised him, Shu said sternly, "Men are not Yao or Shun—how can every matter be wholly good!"

sentences.zh: 導改容謝之。

translations.literal: Dao changed expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Dao changed expression and apologized.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎南遊，臨江而還。

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao toured south, came to the river, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: King Hu of Zhao toured south, came to the Yangzi, and returned.

sentences.zh: 有游騎十餘至歷陽，歷陽太守袁耽表上之，不言騎多少。

translations.literal: More than ten roaming horsemen reached Liyang; Liyang Administrator Yuan Dan memorialized upward but did not state how many horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten roaming horsemen reached Liyang; Liyang Administrator Yuan Dan memorialized the court but did not state how many horsemen there were.

sentences.zh: 朝廷震懼，司徒導請出討之。

translations.literal: The court was shaken with alarm; Minister of Education Dao requested to go out and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was shaken with alarm; Minister of Education Wang Dao asked to lead a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，加導大司馬、假黃鉞、都督征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Dao was given the additional titles Grand Marshal, with the ceremonial axe lent to him, and Commander-in-Chief for the punitive campaign over all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Dao was made Grand Marshal, lent the ceremonial axe, and appointed Commander-in-Chief of the punitive campaign over all armies.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝觀兵廣莫門，分命諸將救歷陽及戍慈湖、牛渚、蕪湖；

translations.literal: On guichou the Emperor reviewed troops at the Gate of Broad Apocalypse, assigning generals to relieve Liyang and to garrison Cihu, Niuzhu, and Wuhu;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the Emperor reviewed troops at the Gate of Broad Apocalypse, assigning generals to relieve Liyang and to garrison Cihu, Niuzhu, and Wuhu;

sentences.zh: 司空郗鑒使廣陵相陳光將兵入衛京師。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chi Jian sent Administrator of Guangling Chen Guang with troops to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chi Jian sent Administrator of Guangling Chen Guang with troops to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄聞趙騎至少，又已去，戊午，解嚴，王導解大司馬。

translations.literal: Soon they heard the Zhao horsemen were few and had already gone; on wuwu the emergency was lifted and Wang Dao resigned as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they heard the Zhao horsemen were few and had already departed; on wuwu the emergency was lifted and Wang Dao resigned as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 袁耽坐輕妄免官。

translations.literal: Yuan Dan was dismissed from office for frivolous alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dan was dismissed from office for reckless alarm.

sentences.zh: 趙征虜將軍石遇攻桓宣於襄陽，不克。

translations.literal: The Zhao general Who Conquers the Barbarians Shi Yu attacked Huan Xuan at Xiangyang and did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao general Who Conquers the Barbarians, Shi Yu, attacked Huan Xuan at Xiangyang and failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 大旱，會稽、餘姚米斗五百。

translations.literal: Great drought; in Kuaiji and Yuyao rice was five hundred cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck; in Kuaiji and Yuyao rice sold for five hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，慕容皝立子俊為世子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Murong Huang installed his son Jun as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Murong Huang installed his son Murong Jun as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙王虎遷都於鄴，大赦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month King Hu of Zhao moved the capital to Ye and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month King Hu of Zhao moved the capital to Ye and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，趙主勒以天竺僧佛圖澄豫言成敗，數有驗，敬事之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao ruler Le had honored the Tianzhu monk Fotudeng, who foretold success and failure and was repeatedly proved right.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Zhao ruler Shi Le had honored the Indian monk Fotudeng, who foretold success and failure and was repeatedly proved right.

sentences.zh: 及虎即位，奉之尤謹，衣以綾錦，乘以雕輦。

translations.literal: When Hu came to the throne he venerated him all the more strictly, clothing him in damask and brocade and having him ride in a carved carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu came to the throne he venerated him all the more strictly, clothing him in damask and brocade and having him ride in a carved palanquin.

sentences.zh: 朝會之日，太子、諸公扶翼上殿，主者唱「大和尚」，眾坐皆起。

translations.literal: On days of court assembly the crown prince and the princes supported him on both sides up the hall; the usher proclaimed "Great Monk," and all seated rose.
translations.idiomatic: On days of court assembly the crown prince and the princes supported him on both sides up the hall; the usher proclaimed "Great Monk," and all those seated rose.

sentences.zh: 使司空李農旦夕問起居，太子、諸公五日一朝。

translations.literal: He had Minister of Works Li Nong inquire morning and evening after his health; the crown prince and the princes attended court once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: He had Minister of Works Li Nong inquire morning and evening after his health; the crown prince and the princes attended court once every five days.

sentences.zh: 國人化之，率多事佛。

translations.literal: The people of the realm were transformed by this and mostly took up Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the realm were transformed by this and mostly took up Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 澄之所在，無敢向其方面涕唾者。

translations.literal: Where Chen was, none dared to weep tears or spit in his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Where Fotudeng was, none dared weep or spit in his direction.

sentences.zh: 爭造寺廟，削髮出家。

translations.literal: They vied to build temples and shaved their heads to leave home.
translations.idiomatic: They vied to build temples and shaved their heads to become monks.

sentences.zh: 虎以其真偽雜糅，或避賦役為奸宄，乃下詔問中書曰：「佛，國家所奉。

translations.literal: Hu, because the genuine and false were mixed and some evaded taxes and corvée to become outlaws, issued an edict asking the Secretariat: "The Buddha is what the state reveres.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, because genuine and false believers were mixed and some evaded taxes and corvée to become outlaws, issued an edict asking the Secretariat, "The Buddha is what the state reveres.

sentences.zh: 里閭小人無爵秩者，應事佛不？」

translations.literal: Should petty men of the lanes and hamlets without rank and title serve the Buddha or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Should commoners of the lanes and hamlets without rank and title serve the Buddha or not?"

sentences.zh: 著作郎王度等議曰：「王者祭祀，典禮具存。

translations.literal: Gentleman of Monographs Wang Du and others deliberated: "Kings have sacrifices—the canonical rites fully exist.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of Monographs Wang Du and others deliberated, "Kings have sacrifices—the canonical rites fully exist.

sentences.zh: 佛，外國之神，非天子諸華所應祠奉。

translations.literal: The Buddha is a god of foreign lands, not what the Son of Heaven and the various Hua ought to worship.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha is a god of foreign lands, not what the Son of Heaven and the Hua peoples ought to worship.

sentences.zh: 漢氏初傳其道，唯聽西域人立寺都邑以奉之，漢人皆不得出家；

translations.literal: When the Han first transmitted this Way, only Western Regions people were permitted to erect temples in capital and commandery to serve it; Han people were all forbidden to leave home;
translations.idiomatic: When the Han first transmitted this Way, only Western Regions people were permitted to erect temples in capitals and commanderies to serve it; Han people were all forbidden to become monks;

sentences.zh: 魏世亦然。

translations.literal: the Wei age was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei age was likewise.

sentences.zh: 今宜禁公卿以下毋得詣寺燒香、禮拜；

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to forbid those below the public ministers from going to temples to burn incense and perform obeisance;
translations.idiomatic: Now it is fitting to forbid those below the rank of public minister from going to temples to burn incense and perform obeisance;

sentences.zh: 其趙人為沙門者，皆返初服。」

translations.literal: those Zhao people who are monks should all return to their original garments."
translations.idiomatic: those Zhao people who are monks should all return to lay dress."

sentences.zh: 虎詔曰：「朕生自邊鄙，忝君諸夏，至於饗祀，應從本俗。

translations.literal: Hu's edict said: "I was born from the border marches and am honored to rule the various Xia—as to offerings and sacrifices, I ought to follow my native custom.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's edict said, "I was born on the frontier and am honored to rule the Central States—as to offerings and sacrifices, I ought to follow my native custom.

sentences.zh: 其夷、趙百姓樂事佛者，特聽之。」

translations.literal: Those among the Yi and Zhao common people who delighted in serving the Buddha were specially permitted to do so."
translations.idiomatic: Those among the tribal peoples and Zhao commoners who wished to serve the Buddha were specially permitted to do so."

sentences.zh: 趙章武王斌帥精騎二萬並秦、雍二州兵以討薄句大，平之。

translations.literal: The Zhao Prince of Zhangwu Bin led twenty thousand elite cavalry together with the armies of Qin and Yong provinces to attack Bo Gou Da and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Prince of Zhangwu, Shi Bin, led twenty thousand elite cavalry together with the armies of Qin and Yong provinces to attack Bo Gou Da and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 成太子班之舅羅演，與漢王相天水上官澹謀殺成主期，立班子。

translations.literal: Luo Yan, maternal uncle of the Cheng crown prince Ban, plotted with the Han king's chancellor Shangguan Dan of Tianshui to kill the Cheng ruler Qi and install Ban's son.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yan, maternal uncle of the Cheng crown prince Ban, plotted with Shangguan Dan, chancellor to the Han king in Tianshui, to kill the Cheng ruler Li Qi and install Ban's son.

sentences.zh: 事覺，期殺演、澹及班母羅氏。

translations.literal: When the plot was discovered, Qi killed Yan, Dan, and Ban's mother the Lady Luo.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Qi executed Yan, Dan, and Ban's mother Lady Luo.

sentences.zh: 期自以得志，輕諸舊臣，信任尚書令景騫、尚書姚華、田褒、中常侍許涪等，刑賞大政，皆決於數人，希復關公卿。

translations.literal: Qi, thinking himself triumphant, slighted the old ministers and trusted Director of the Masters of Writing Jing Qian, Masters of Writing Yao Hua, Tian Bao, Palace Attendant Xu Fu, and others; great matters of punishment and reward were all decided by a few men, seldom involving the public ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, flush with success, slighted the old ministers and trusted Director of the Masters of Writing Jing Qian, Masters of Writing Yao Hua and Tian Bao, and Palace Attendant Xu Fu; major punishments and rewards were decided by a handful of men, seldom brought before the full court.

sentences.zh: 褒無它才，嘗勸成主雄立期為太子，故有寵。

translations.literal: Bao had no other talent; he had once urged the Cheng ruler Xiong to install Qi as crown prince, and therefore enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had no other talent; he had once urged the Cheng ruler Li Xiong to name Qi crown prince, and therefore enjoyed favor.

sentences.zh: 由是紀綱隳紊，雄業始衰。

translations.literal: From this the laws and discipline were ruined and disordered, and Xiong's enterprise began to decline.
translations.idiomatic: From this the laws and discipline collapsed, and the Cheng enterprise began to decline.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyi the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyi the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 慕容仁遣王齊等南還。

translations.literal: Murong Ren sent Wang Qi and others south to return.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ren sent Wang Qi and others south on their return journey.

sentences.zh: 齊等自海道趣棘城，齊遇風不至。

translations.literal: Qi and the others took the sea route toward Jicheng; Qi met contrary winds and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others took the sea route toward Jicheng, but Qi met contrary winds and failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 十二月，徐孟等至棘城，慕容皝始受朝命。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xu Meng and the others reached Jicheng, and Murong Huang at last received the court's commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xu Meng and the others reached Jicheng, and Murong Huang at last received the court's commission.

sentences.zh: 段氏、宇文氏各遣使詣慕容仁，館於平郭城外。

translations.literal: The Duan and Yuwenshi each sent envoys to Murong Ren, lodging outside Pingguo city.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan and Yuwen clans each sent envoys to Murong Ren, lodging outside Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 皝帳下督張英將百餘騎間道潛行掩擊之，斬宇文氏使十餘人，生擒段氏使以歸。

translations.literal: Huang's camp supervisor Zhang Ying led more than a hundred horsemen by a hidden path in a stealthy raid, beheading more than ten envoys of the Yuwenshi and capturing the Duan envoys alive to bring back.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's camp supervisor Zhang Ying led more than a hundred horsemen by a hidden path in a surprise raid, beheading more than ten Yuwen envoys and capturing the Duan envoys alive.

sentences.zh: 是歲，明帝母建安君荀氏卒。

translations.literal: That year the mother of Emperor Ming, Lady Jian'an Jun of the Xun clan, died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lady Jian'an Jun of the Xun clan, mother of Emperor Ming, died.

sentences.zh: 荀氏在禁中，尊重同於太后；

translations.literal: Lady Xun within the forbidden quarters was honored the same as an empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xun within the palace precincts was honored as an empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 詔贈豫章郡君。

translations.literal: an edict posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: an edict posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 代王翳槐以賀蘭藹頭不恭，將召而戮之，諸部皆叛。

translations.literal: The Dai king Yihua, because Helan Aitou was disrespectful, was about to summon and execute him; all the tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Yihua, because Helan Aitou had been disrespectful, was about to summon and execute him; all the tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 代王紇那自宇文部入，諸部復奉之。

translations.literal: The Dai king Hena entered from the Yuwen tribe, and the tribes again upheld him.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Hena entered from the Yuwen tribe, and the tribes again upheld him.

sentences.zh: 翳槐奔鄴，趙人厚遇之。

translations.literal: Yihua fled to Ye; the Zhao people treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yihua fled to Ye, where the Zhao court treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 初，張軌及二子寔、茂，雖保據河右，而軍旅之事無歲無之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Gui and his two sons Shi and Mao, though they held the lands west of the Yellow River, had military campaigns year after year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Gui and his sons Shi and Mao, though they held the lands west of the Yellow River, faced military campaigns every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 及張駿嗣位，境內漸平。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun succeeded to the throne, within the borders peace gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun succeeded, peace gradually returned within his borders.

sentences.zh: 駿勤修庶政，總御文武，鹹得其用，民富兵強，遠近稱之，以為賢君。

translations.literal: Jun diligently cultivated ordinary government, marshaled civil and military officials, and all were put to good use; the people grew rich and the army strong; near and far praised him as a worthy ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Jun diligently governed, marshaled civil and military officials to their best use, and made the people rich and the army strong; near and far praised him as a worthy ruler.

sentences.zh: 駿遣將楊宣伐龜茲、鄯善，於是西域諸國焉耆、于闐之屬，皆詣姑臧朝貢。

translations.literal: Jun sent the general Yang Xuan to attack Kucha and Shanshan; thereupon the Western Regions states including Yanqi and Yutian all came to Guzang to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent General Yang Xuan to attack Kucha and Shanshan; thereafter the Western Regions states, including Yanqi and Yutian, all came to Guzang to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 駿於姑臧南作五殿，官屬皆稱臣。

translations.literal: Jun built five halls south of Guzang, and his officials all styled themselves ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun built five halls south of Guzang, and his officials all styled themselves his ministers.

sentences.zh: 駿有兼秦、雍之志，遣參軍麴護上疏，以為：「勒、雄既死，虎、期繼逆，兆庶離主，漸冉經世；

translations.literal: Jun harbored ambitions to seize Qin and Yong and sent his aide Qu Hu to submit a memorial, arguing: "Le and Xiong are already dead; Hu and Qi succeed in rebellion; the myriad people are separated from their lord, and year by year the age passes;
translations.idiomatic: Jun harbored ambitions to seize Qin and Yong and sent his aide Qu Hu to submit a memorial arguing, "Le and Xiong are dead; Hu and Qi succeed them in rebellion; the people are cut off from their sovereign, and the years slip away;

sentences.zh: 先老消落，後生不識，慕戀之心，日遠日忘。

translations.literal: the elders of old fade and fall; those born later do not know; the heart's longing and attachment grows daily more distant and forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: the elders die off, the young no longer remember, and longing for the throne grows daily more distant and forgotten.

sentences.zh: 乞敕司空鑒、征西亮等泛舟江、沔，首尾齊舉。」

translations.literal: I beg that you command Minister of Works Jian, General Who Conquers the West Liang, and others to float boats on the Jiang and Han, striking in concert from head to tail."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty command Minister of Works Chi Jian, General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang, and others to sail the Yangzi and Han rivers and strike in concert from both ends."

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹康二年（

translations.literal: Middle upper section under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, second year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, middle period upper section, second year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元三三六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, CE 336)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, CE 336)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，彗星見於奎、婁。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi a comet appeared in the constellations Kui and Lou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi a comet appeared in the constellations Kui and Lou.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝將討慕容仁，司馬高詡曰：「仁叛棄君親，民神怒；

translations.literal: Murong Huang was about to campaign against Murong Ren; Major Gao Xu said: "Ren betrayed his lord and kin; the people and spirits are angry;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang was about to campaign against Murong Ren. Major Gao Xu said, "Ren betrayed his lord and kin; the people and spirits are angry;

sentences.zh: 前此海未嘗凍，自仁反以來，連年凍者三矣。

translations.literal: before this the sea had never frozen; since Ren's rebellion it has frozen three years in succession.
translations.idiomatic: before this the sea had never frozen; since Ren's rebellion it has frozen three years running.

sentences.zh: 且仁專備陸道，天其或者欲使吾乘海冰以襲之也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Ren concentrates his defenses on the land routes—perhaps Heaven wishes us to cross the frozen sea to strike him."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ren concentrates his defenses on land routes—perhaps Heaven wishes us to cross the frozen sea to strike him."

sentences.zh: 皝從之。

translations.literal: Huang followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Huang followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 群僚皆言涉冰危事，不若從陸道。

translations.literal: The assembled officials all said crossing the ice was perilous and it would be better to take the land route.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled officials all said crossing the ice was perilous and urged the land route instead.

sentences.zh: 皝曰：「吾計已決，敢沮者斬！」

translations.literal: Huang said: "My plan is already settled—whoever dares discourage it, behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Huang said, "My plan is settled—whoever dares discourage it will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 壬午，皝帥其弟軍師將軍評等自昌黎東，踐冰而進，凡三百餘里。

translations.literal: On renwu Huang led his younger brother the Army Strategist General Ping and others east from Changli, treading the ice as they advanced more than three hundred li in all.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Huang led his younger brother the Army Strategist General Murong Ping and others east from Changli, marching over the ice for more than three hundred li in all.

sentences.zh: 至歷林口，捨輜重，輕兵趣平郭。

translations.literal: Reaching Lilin Ford they abandoned baggage trains and with light troops hastened to Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Lilin Ford they abandoned their baggage trains and hurried to Pingguo with light troops.

sentences.zh: 去城七里，候騎以告仁，仁狼狽出戰。

translations.literal: Seven li from the city, scouts reported to Ren; Ren rushed out to battle in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Seven li from the city, scouts reported to Ren, and Ren rushed out to battle in disarray.

sentences.zh: 張英之俘二使也，仁恨不窮追；

translations.literal: When Zhang Ying had captured the two envoys, Ren regretted not pursuing to the end;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ying had captured the two envoys, Ren regretted not pursuing to the end;

sentences.zh: 及皝至，仁以為皝復遣偏師輕出寇抄，不知皝自來，謂左右曰：「今茲當不使其匹馬得返矣！」

translations.literal: when Huang arrived Ren thought Huang had again sent a detached force on a light raid and did not know Huang had come in person; he said to those beside him: "This time not a single horse of theirs shall return!"
translations.idiomatic: when Huang arrived Ren thought he had sent only a detached raiding force and did not know Huang had come in person; he told his attendants, "This time not one of their horses shall return!"

sentences.zh: 乙未，仁悉眾陳於城之西北。

translations.literal: On yiyi Ren arrayed his entire force northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyi Ren arrayed his entire force northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 慕容軍帥所部降於皝，仁眾沮動；

translations.literal: Murong Jun led his command in surrender to Huang; Ren's host was dismayed and shaken;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun led his command in surrender to Huang; Ren's army was dismayed and shaken;

sentences.zh: 皝從而縱擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Huang followed with a full assault and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Huang followed with a full assault and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 仁走，其帳下皆叛，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Ren fled; his personal followers all rebelled, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ren fled; his personal followers all deserted, and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 皝先為斬其帳下之叛者，然後賜仁死。

translations.literal: Huang first had the rebels among his followers beheaded, then granted Ren death.
translations.idiomatic: Huang first had Ren's deserters beheaded, then granted Ren death.

sentences.zh: 丁衡、游毅、孫機等，皆仁所信用也，皝執而斬之；

translations.literal: Ding Heng, You Yi, Sun Ji, and others, all men Ren had trusted, Huang seized and beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Heng, You Yi, Sun Ji, and others, all men Ren had trusted, Huang seized and beheaded;

sentences.zh: 王冰自殺。

translations.literal: Wang Bing killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bing killed himself.

sentences.zh: 慕容幼、慕容稚、佟壽、郭充、翟楷、龐鑒皆東走，幼中道而還；

translations.literal: Murong You, Murong Zhi, Tong Shou, Guo Chong, Zhai Kai, and Pang Jian all fled east; You turned back midway;
translations.idiomatic: Murong You, Murong Zhi, Tong Shou, Guo Chong, Zhai Kai, and Pang Jian all fled east; You turned back midway;

sentences.zh: 皝兵追及楷、鑒，斬之；

translations.literal: Huang's troops overtook Kai and Jian and beheaded them;
translations.idiomatic: Huang's troops overtook Kai and Jian and beheaded them;

sentences.zh: 壽、充奔高麗。

translations.literal: Shou and Chong fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Shou and Chong fled to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 自餘吏民為仁所詿誤者，皝皆赦之。

translations.literal: All remaining officials and commoners misled by Ren, Huang pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang pardoned all remaining officials and commoners misled by Ren.

sentences.zh: 封高詡為汝陽侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Gao Xu as Marquis of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Gao Xu as Marquis of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，尚書僕射王彬卒。

translations.literal: In the second month Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Bin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Bin died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，帝臨軒，遣使備六禮逆故當陽侯杜乂女陵陽為皇后，大赦；

translations.literal: On xinhai the Emperor presided at the hall, sent envoys with the six rites to escort the former Marquis of Dangyang Du Yi's daughter Lingyang as empress, and proclaimed a general amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Emperor presided at court, sent envoys with the six rites to escort Lingyang, daughter of the former Marquis of Dangyang Du Yi, as empress, and proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 群臣畢賀。

translations.literal: the assembled ministers all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: the assembled ministers all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，段遼遣中軍將軍李詠襲慕容皝。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Duan Liao sent Central Army General Li Yong to raid Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, Duan Liao sent Central Army General Li Yong to raid Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 詠趣武興，都尉張萌擊擒之。

translations.literal: Yong hastened to Wuxing; Commandant Zhang Meng attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong hastened to Wuxing; Commandant Zhang Meng attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 遼別遣段蘭將步騎數萬屯柳城西回水，宇文逸豆歸攻安晉以為蘭聲援。

translations.literal: Liao separately sent Duan Lan with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to encamp at Xihui River west of Liucheng; Yuwenshi Yidougui attacked Anjin to support Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao separately sent Duan Lan with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to encamp at Xihui River west of Liucheng, while Yuwen Yidougui attacked Anjin to support Lan.

sentences.zh: 皝帥步騎五萬向柳城，蘭不戰而遁。

translations.literal: Huang led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Liucheng; Lan fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Huang led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Liucheng; Lan fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 皝引兵北趣安晉，逸豆歸棄輜重走；

translations.literal: Huang led his troops north toward Anjin; Yidougui abandoned baggage trains and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Huang led his troops north toward Anjin; Yidougui abandoned his baggage trains and fled;

sentences.zh: 皝遣司馬封弈帥輕騎追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Huang sent Major Feng Yi with light cavalry in pursuit and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Huang sent Major Feng Yi with light cavalry in pursuit and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 皝謂諸將曰：「二虜恥無功，必將復至，宜於柳城左右設伏以待之。」

translations.literal: Huang said to the generals: "The two barbarians, shamed at achieving nothing, are sure to come again—you ought to set ambushes around Liucheng and wait for them."
translations.idiomatic: Huang told his generals, "The two barbarian leaders, shamed at achieving nothing, are sure to return—you should set ambushes around Liucheng and wait for them."

sentences.zh: 乃遣封弈帥騎數千伏於馬兜山。

translations.literal: He then sent Feng Yi with several thousand horsemen to lie in wait on Madou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Feng Yi with several thousand horsemen to lie in wait on Madou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 三月，段遼果將數千騎來寇抄。

translations.literal: In the third month Duan Liao indeed led several thousand horsemen on a raiding attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Duan Liao indeed led several thousand horsemen on a raiding attack.

sentences.zh: 弈縱擊，大破之，斬其將榮伯保。

translations.literal: Yi loosed a full assault and routed them utterly, beheading their general Rong Bobao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi launched a full assault and routed them, beheading their general Rong Bobao.

sentences.zh: 前廷尉孔坦卒。

translations.literal: The former Commandant of Justice Kong Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: The former Commandant of Justice Kong Tan died.

sentences.zh: 坦疾篤，庾冰省之，流涕。

translations.literal: Tan was gravely ill; Yu Bing visited him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was gravely ill; Yu Bing visited him and wept.

sentences.zh: 坦慨然曰：「大丈夫將終，不問以濟國安民之術，乃為兒女子相泣邪！」

translations.literal: Tan said with feeling: "When a great man is about to die, you do not ask him the arts of saving the state and settling the people, yet you weep together like children!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said sternly, "When a great man is about to die, you do not ask him how to save the state and settle the people, yet you weep together like children!"

sentences.zh: 冰深謝之。

translations.literal: Bing apologized deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Bing apologized deeply.

sentences.zh: 九月，慕容皝遣長史劉斌、兼郎中令遼東陽景送徐孟等還建康。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Murong Huang sent Chief Clerk Liu Bin and acting Gentlemen-Ordinary of the Palace, Yang Jing of Liaodong, to escort Xu Meng and the others back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Murong Huang sent Chief Clerk Liu Bin and acting Gentlemen-Ordinary of the Palace Yang Jing of Liaodong to escort Xu Meng and the others back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，廣州刺史鄧岳遣督護王隨等擊夜郎、興古，皆克之；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Governor of Guangzhou Deng Yue sent Supervisor Wang Sui and others to attack Yelang and Xinggu, and both were taken;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Governor of Guangzhou Deng Yue sent Supervisor Wang Sui and others to attack Yelang and Xinggu, and both were conquered;

sentences.zh: 加岳督寧州。

translations.literal: Yue was given additional oversight of Ning province.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was given additional oversight of Ning province.

sentences.zh: 成主期以從子尚書僕射武陵公載有俊才，忌之，誣以謀反，殺之。

translations.literal: The Cheng ruler Qi, because his cousin Vice Director of the Masters of Writing the Duke of Wuling Zai had outstanding talent, envied him, falsely charged him with plotting rebellion, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng ruler Li Qi, envying his cousin Vice Director of the Masters of Writing the Duke of Wuling Li Zai for his outstanding talent, falsely charged him with plotting rebellion and killed him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔建威將軍司馬勳將兵安集漢中；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict ordered General Who Establishes Might Sima Xun to lead troops to settle and gather Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict ordered General Who Establishes Might Sima Xun to lead troops to pacify Hanzhong;

sentences.zh: 成漢王壽擊敗之。

translations.literal: the Cheng-Han king Shou defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: the Cheng-Han king Li Shou defeated him.

sentences.zh: 壽遂置漢中守宰，戍南鄭而還。

translations.literal: Shou then installed administrators for Hanzhong, garrisoned Nanzheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then installed administrators in Hanzhong, garrisoned Nanzheng, and returned.

sentences.zh: 索頭郁鞠帥眾三萬降於趙，趙拜郁鞠等十三人為親趙王，散其部眾於冀、青等六州。

translations.literal: Suotou Yuju led thirty thousand followers in surrender to Zhao; Zhao invested Yuju and twelve others as Princes Who Are Kin to Zhao and dispersed their followers through the six provinces including Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Suotou Yuju led thirty thousand followers in surrender to Zhao; Zhao invested Yuju and twelve others as Princes Kin to Zhao and dispersed their followers through six provinces including Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎作太武殿於襄國，作東、西宮於鄴，十二月，皆成。

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao built the Hall of Grand Martiality at Xiangguo and the Eastern and Western Palaces at Ye; in the twelfth month all were completed.
translations.idiomatic: King Hu of Zhao built the Hall of Grand Martiality at Xiangguo and the Eastern and Western Palaces at Ye; in the twelfth month all were completed.

sentences.zh: 太武殿基高二丈八尺，縱六十五步，廣七十五步，甃以文石。

translations.literal: The Hall of Grand Martiality's foundation was two zhang eight chi high, sixty-five paces long and seventy-five paces wide, paved with patterned stone.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Grand Martiality's foundation was two zhang eight chi high, sixty-five paces long and seventy-five paces wide, paved with patterned stone.

sentences.zh: 下穿伏室，置衛士五百人。

translations.literal: Below it were dug hidden chambers with five hundred guards stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Below it were dug hidden chambers with five hundred guards stationed.

sentences.zh: 以漆灌瓦，金璫，銀楹，珠簾，玉壁，窮極工巧。

translations.literal: Roof tiles were lacquered, with gold finials, silver pillars, pearl curtains, and jade disks—craftsmanship pushed to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Roof tiles were lacquered; gold finials, silver pillars, pearl curtains, and jade disks pushed craftsmanship to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 殿上施白玉床、流蘇帳，為金蓮華以冠帳頂。

translations.literal: On the hall was set a white jade bed and a fringe canopy, topped with a golden lotus crowning the canopy peak.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall stood a white jade bed and a fringe canopy crowned with a golden lotus at its peak.

sentences.zh: 又作九殿於顯陽殿後，選士民之女以實之，服珠玉、被綺縠者萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also built nine halls behind the Hall of Manifest Yang, selecting daughters of gentry and commoners to fill them; more than ten thousand wore pearls and jade and were clad in fine silks.
translations.idiomatic: He also built nine halls behind the Hall of Manifest Yang, selecting daughters of gentry and commoners to fill them; more than ten thousand wore pearls and jade and fine silks.

sentences.zh: 教宮人占星氣、馬步射。

translations.literal: He taught palace women to read astral signs and to shoot from horseback and on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He taught palace women to read astral signs and to shoot from horseback and on foot.

sentences.zh: 置女太史，及雜伎工巧，皆與外同。

translations.literal: He installed female grand astrologers and miscellaneous performers and artisans, all the same as outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He installed female grand astrologers and miscellaneous performers and artisans, mirroring those outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 以女騎千人為鹵簿，皆著紫綸巾，熟錦褲，金銀鏤帶，五文織成靴，執羽儀，鳴鼓吹，游宴以自隨。

translations.literal: He took a thousand female riders as his guard of honor, all wearing purple silk caps, brocade trousers, gold and silver inlaid belts, five-colored woven boots; bearing feather standards, sounding drums and pipes, they accompanied him on his pleasure outings.
translations.idiomatic: He took a thousand female riders as his guard of honor, all wearing purple silk caps, brocade trousers, gold and silver inlaid belts, and five-colored woven boots; bearing feather standards and sounding drums and pipes, they accompanied him on his pleasure outings.

sentences.zh: 於是趙大旱，金一斤直粟二鬥，百姓嗷然；

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao suffered great drought; one jin of gold was worth two dou of grain; the common people wailed;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao suffered a great drought; one jin of gold was worth two dou of grain, and the people wailed in distress;

sentences.zh: 而虎用兵不息，百役並興。

translations.literal: yet Hu's use of troops never ceased and a hundred corvées arose together.
translations.idiomatic: yet Hu's campaigns never ceased and a hundred corvées arose together.

sentences.zh: 使牙門將張彌行徙洛陽鐘虡、九龍、翁仲、銅駝、飛廉於鄴，載以四輪纏輞車，轍廣四尺，深二尺。

translations.literal: He sent Gate General Zhang Mi to move Luoyang's bell stands, Nine Dragons, Wengzhong statues, bronze camels, and Feilian figures to Ye, loading them on four-wheeled wagons with wrapped rims; the ruts were four chi wide and two chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gate General Zhang Mi to move Luoyang's bell stands, Nine Dragons, Wengzhong statues, bronze camels, and Feilian figures to Ye, loading them on four-wheeled wagons with wrapped rims; the ruts were four chi wide and two chi deep.

sentences.zh: 一鐘沒於河，募浮沒三百人入河，系以竹絲亙，用牛百頭，鹿櫨引之，乃出，造萬斛之舟以濟之。

translations.literal: One bell sank in the river; he recruited three hundred divers to enter the river, bound it with bamboo cords stretched across, used a hundred oxen and a capstan to draw it out, then built ten-thousand-bushel boats to ferry it across.
translations.idiomatic: One bell sank in the river; he recruited three hundred divers, bound it with bamboo cords stretched across, used a hundred oxen and a capstan to draw it out, then built ten-thousand-bushel boats to ferry it across.

sentences.zh: 既至鄴，虎大悅，為之赦二歲刑，賚百官谷帛，賜民爵一級。

translations.literal: When they reached Ye, Hu was greatly pleased and for this granted amnesty for crimes up to two years' punishment, bestowed grain and silk on the hundred officials, and granted the people one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Ye, Hu was greatly pleased and granted amnesty for crimes up to two years' punishment, bestowed grain and silk on officials, and granted the people one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 又用尚方令解飛之言，於鄴南投石於河，以作飛橋，功費數千萬億，橋竟不成，役夫饑甚，乃止。

translations.literal: He also followed Palace Workshop Director Xie Fei's advice to cast stones into the river south of Ye to build a flying bridge; the labor cost tens of millions; the bridge in the end was not completed; the corvée laborers were desperately hungry, and he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Palace Workshop Director Xie Fei's advice to cast stones into the river south of Ye to build a flying bridge; the labor cost tens of millions; the bridge was never completed; the corvée laborers were desperately hungry, and he then stopped.

sentences.zh: 使令長帥民入山澤采橡及魚以佐食，復為權豪所奪，民無所得。

translations.literal: He had magistrates lead the people into mountains and marshes to gather acorns and fish to supplement food, but these were again seized by powerful families, and the people gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He had magistrates lead the people into mountains and marshes to gather acorns and fish to supplement their food, but powerful families seized the harvest and the people gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 初，日南夷帥范稚，有奴曰範文，常隨商賈往來中國；

translations.literal: Earlier, the chief of Rinan among the Yi, Fan Zhi, had a slave named Fan Wen who often followed merchants traveling to China;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Zhi, chief of the Yi in Rinan, had a slave named Fan Wen who often followed merchants to China;

sentences.zh: 後至林邑，教林邑王范逸作城郭、宮室、器械，逸愛信之，使為將。

translations.literal: later he reached Linyi and taught King Fan Yi of Linyi to build walls, palaces, and weapons; Yi loved and trusted him and made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: later he reached Linyi and taught King Fan Yi of Linyi to build walls, palaces, and weapons; Yi loved and trusted him and made him a general.

sentences.zh: 文遂譖逸諸子，或徙或逃。

translations.literal: Wen then slandered Yi's sons, and they were either relocated or fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then slandered Yi's sons until they were either relocated or fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，逸卒，文詐迎逸子於它國，置毒於椰酒而殺之，文自立為王。

translations.literal: That year Yi died; Wen falsely welcomed Yi's son from another state, put poison in coconut wine and killed him, and Wen installed himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fan Yi died; Fan Wen falsely welcomed Yi's son from another state, poisoned his coconut wine, and killed him, then installed himself as king.

sentences.zh: 於是出兵攻大岐界、小岐界、式僕、徐狼、屈都、乾魯、扶單等國，皆滅之，有眾四五萬，遣使奉表入貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent troops to attack the states of Daqijie, Xiaoqijie, Shipu, Xulang, Qudu, Ganlu, Fudan, and others, destroying them all; he had forty or fifty thousand followers and sent envoys with memorials to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops to attack Daqijie, Xiaoqijie, Shipu, Xulang, Qudu, Ganlu, Fudan, and other states, destroying them all; he had forty or fifty thousand followers and sent envoys with memorials to pay tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 趙左校令成公段作庭燎於槓末，高十餘丈，上盤置燎，下盤置人，趙王虎試而悅之。

translations.literal: The Zhao Left Commandant of the Guard Cheng Gong Duan built a court beacon at the end of a pole more than ten zhang high, with the beacon on the upper platform and men on the lower; King Hu of Zhao tested it and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Left Commandant of the Guard Cheng Gong Duan built a court beacon on a pole more than ten zhang high, with the beacon on the upper platform and men on the lower; King Hu tested it and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝中之上鹹康三年（

translations.literal: Middle upper section under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, third year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the Illustrious Ancestor, middle period upper section, third year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元三三七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, CE 337)
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, CE 337)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚辰，趙太保夔安等文武五百餘人入上尊號，庭燎油灌下盤，死者二十餘人；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengchen more than five hundred civil and military officials including Zhao Grand Guardian Kui An presented the exalted title; oil from the court beacon poured onto the lower platform and more than twenty died;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengchen more than five hundred civil and military officials including Zhao Grand Guardian Kui An presented the exalted title; oil from the court beacon poured onto the lower platform and more than twenty died;

sentences.zh: 趙王虎惡之，腰斬成公段。

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao detested this and had Cheng Gong Duan cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: King Hu detested this and had Cheng Gong Duan cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，虎依殷、周之制，稱大趙天王，即位於南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi Hu followed the institutions of Yin and Zhou, styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao, took the throne at the southern suburb, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Hu followed the institutions of Yin and Zhou, styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao, took the throne at the southern suburb, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 立其後鄭氏為天王皇后，太子邃為天王皇太子，諸子為王者皆降為郡公，宗室為王者降為縣侯。

translations.literal: He installed his consort the Lady Zheng as Heavenly King Queen, Crown Prince Sui as Heavenly King Crown Prince; sons who had been kings were all demoted to dukes of commanderies, and kinsmen who had been kings were demoted to marquises of counties.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his consort Lady Zheng as Heavenly King Queen and Crown Prince Shi Sui as Heavenly King Crown Prince; sons who had been kings were demoted to dukes of commanderies, and royal kinsmen who had been kings were demoted to marquises of counties.

sentences.zh: 百官封署各有差。

translations.literal: The hundred officials received enfeoffments and appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials received enfeoffments and appointments according to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒袁瑰、太常馮懷，以江左浸安，請興學校，帝從之。

translations.literal: Libationer of the Imperial Academy Yuan Gui and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Feng Huai, because the lands south of the Yangzi were gradually secure, requested the founding of schools; the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer of the Imperial Academy Yuan Gui and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Feng Huai, because the lands south of the Yangzi were gradually secure, requested the founding of schools; the Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，立太學，徵集生徒。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Imperial University was established and students were summoned and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Imperial University was established and students were summoned.

sentences.zh: 而士大夫習尚老、莊，儒術終不振。

translations.literal: Yet the gentry and officials were devoted to Laozi and Zhuangzi, and Confucian learning in the end did not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentry favored Laozi and Zhuangzi, and Confucian learning never truly flourished.

sentences.zh: 瑰，渙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Gui was the great-grandson of Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was the great-grandson of Yuan Huan.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容皝於乙連城東築好城以逼乙連，留折衝將軍蘭勃守之。

translations.literal: In the third month Murong Huang built Haocheng east of Yiliancheng to press Yilian, leaving Breaker of Charges General Lan Bo to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Murong Huang built Haocheng east of Yiliancheng to press Yilian, leaving Breaker of Charges General Lan Bo to defend it.
